simetri.shapes.shape

Shape: the primary geometric drawable in Simetri.

Create a Shape from a sequence of (x, y) points. Optional style arguments control fill, stroke, markers, and related rendering options. Boolean helpers such as clip, polygon_diff, and polygon_xor operate on closed shapes.

Examples:
>>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (50, 0), (25, 40)], closed=True)
>>> _ = tri.translate(40, 0)
>>> tri.vertices
((40.0, 0.0), (90.0, 0.0), (65.0, 40.0))

 106class Shape(Base, CommonStyle):
 107    """Polyline/polygon drawable with style and affine transform state.
 108
 109    Constructed from a sequence of points. When ``closed`` is True (or the
 110    first and last points coincide), the shape is treated as a polygon for
 111    fill and boolean operations.
 112    If the first and last points coincide then the last point is removed.
 113
 114    Omitted style arguments are stored from ``user_defaults`` at init.
 115    ``color`` and ``alpha`` stay unset unless passed. ``color`` sets both
 116    ``line_color`` and ``fill_color``. ``alpha`` sets both ``line_alpha``
 117    and ``fill_alpha``. Reading a ``line_color`` / ``fill_color`` /
 118    ``line_alpha`` / ``fill_alpha`` that was later set to ``None`` returns
 119    the matching configured default. Use sg.doc(sg.Shape) to see the defaults.
 120
 121    Style color/alpha properties and ``copy_style`` come from ``CommonStyle``.
 122
 123    Attributes:
 124        primary_points: ``Points`` storage.
 125        xform_matrix: 3×3 affine transform (row form).
 126        closed: Whether the outline is closed.
 127        fill / stroke: Draw fill and/or stroke.
 128        line_width / line_color / fill_color: Common style attributes.
 129        subtype: Shape subtype (``Types.SHAPE``, ``Types.CIRCLE``, …).
 130        id: Unique object id.
 131
 132    Examples:
 133        >>> s = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 134        >>> s.vertices
 135        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
 136        >>> s.width
 137        40.0
 138    """

 220        """Initialize a Shape.

 223            points: Vertices as ``(x, y)`` pairs. Defaults to empty.
 224            closed: If True, treat as a closed polygon.
 225            fill: Whether to fill the interior.
 226            stroke: Whether to stroke the outline.
 227            alpha: Overall opacity override.
 228            color: Convenience color (may set fill/line depending on style).
 229            draw_double / draw_fillets / draw_markers: Stroke embellishments.
 230            back_style: Background style enum/value.
 231            double_distance / double_color: Double-line stroke options.
 232            fill_alpha / fill_color / fill_mode: Fill style.
 233            fillet_radius: Corner fillet radius when drawing fillets.
 234            gradient: Optional fill gradient.
 235            line_alpha / line_cap / line_color / line_dash_array /
 236                line_dash_phase / line_join / line_miter_limit / line_width:
 237                Stroke style.
 238            marker_*: Marker drawing options.
 239            even_odd: If True, use even-odd fill rule. Omitted uses
 240                ``user_defaults["even_odd"]`` at init.
 241            markers_only: If True, draw markers without the path.
 242            smooth: Prefer smooth curve rendering when applicable.
 243            subtype: Shape subtype. Defaults to ``Types.SHAPE``.
 244            xform_matrix: Optional initial transform.
 245
 246        Raises:
 247            ValueError: If ``subtype`` is not a ``Types`` member.
 248
 249        Examples:
 250            >>> s = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
 251            >>> s.vertices
 252            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0))
 253            >>> s.closed
 254            True
 255        """

 312    def _clear_geometry_caches(self) -> None:
 313        """Clear cached transformed geometry derived from vertices."""
 314        for attr in (
 315            "_final_coords",
 316            "_vertices",
 317            "_edge_lengths",
 318            "_total_length",
 319        ):
 320            if attr in self.__dict__:
 321                delattr(self, attr)
 322
 323    def _get_closed(
 324        self, points: Sequence[PointType], closed: bool
 325    ) -> tuple[bool, list[PointType]]:
 326        """Determine whether the shape should be considered closed.
 327
 328        Args:
 329            points: Vertices defining the shape.
 330            closed: User-specified closed flag.
 331
 332        Returns:
 333            ``(is_closed, vertices)`` with duplicate closing vertex removed
 334            when detected as a polygon.
 335        """
 336
 337        n = len(points)
 338        if n < 3:
 339            res = False
 340        else:
 341            points = [tuple(x[:2]) for x in points]
 342            polygon = self._is_polygon(points)
 343            res = bool(closed) or polygon
 344            if polygon:
 345                points.pop()
 346        return res, points
 347

 356    def __str__(self) -> str:
 357        """Return a string representation of the shape.
 358
 359        Returns:
 360            str: A string representation of the shape.
 361        """
 362        if len(self.primary_points) == 0:
 363            res = "Shape()"
 364        elif len(self.primary_points) < 4:
 365            res = f"Shape({self.vertices})"
 366        else:
 367            res = f"Shape([{self.vertices[0]}, ..., {self.vertices[-1]}])"
 368        return res

 378    def __getitem__(
 379        self, subscript: int | float | slice
 380    ) -> PointType | list[PointType]:
 381        """Retrieve point(s) from the shape by index or slice.
 382
 383        Args:
 384            subscript: Integer index, fractional index (lerp along an edge),
 385                or slice over transformed vertices.
 386
 387        Returns:
 388            Transformed vertex or list of vertices.
 389
 390        Raises:
 391            TypeError: If the subscript type is invalid.
 392        """
 393        # Use cached final_coords instead of recalculating matrix multiplication
 394        final_coords = self.final_coords
 395
 396        if isinstance(subscript, slice):
 397            res = [tuple(coord[:2]) for coord in final_coords[subscript]]
 398        elif isinstance(subscript, float):
 399            if subscript.is_integer():
 400                subscript = int(subscript)
 401                coord = final_coords[subscript]
 402                res = (coord[0], coord[1])
 403            else:
 404                n = len(final_coords)
 405                index = floor(subscript)
 406                if self.closed:
 407                    next_index = (index + 1) % n
 408                else:
 409                    if subscript >= n - 1:
 410                        raise ValueError("Invalid index!")
 411                    else:
 412                        next_index = index + 1
 413                vertex = final_coords[index]
 414                next_vertex = final_coords[next_index]
 415                t = subscript - index
 416                res = lerp_point(vertex, next_vertex, t)
 417        else:
 418            coord = final_coords[subscript]
 419            res = (coord[0], coord[1])
 420        return res
 421
 422    def __setitem__(
 423        self,
 424        subscript: int | slice,
 425        value: PointType | Sequence[PointType] | Any,
 426    ) -> None:
 427        """Set the point(s) at the given subscript.
 428
 429        Args:
 430            subscript: Index or slice into ``primary_points``.
 431            value: Point(s) in canvas space (inverse-transformed before storage).
 432
 433        Raises:
 434            TypeError: If the subscript type is invalid.
 435        """
 436        if isinstance(subscript, slice):
 437            if is_nested_sequence(value):
 438                value = homogenize(value) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 439            else:
 440                value = homogenize([value]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 441            self.primary_points[
 442                subscript.start : subscript.stop : subscript.step
 443            ] = [tuple(x[:2]) for x in value]
 444            self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = True
 445        elif isinstance(subscript, int):
 446            value = homogenize([value]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 447            self.primary_points[subscript] = tuple(value[0][:2])
 448            self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = True
 449        else:
 450            raise TypeError("Invalid subscript type")
 451        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 452
 453    def __delitem__(self, subscript: int | slice) -> Self:
 454        """Delete the point(s) at the given subscript.
 455
 456        Args:
 457            subscript: Index or slice into ``primary_points``.
 458        """
 459        del self.primary_points[subscript]
 460        self._clear_geometry_caches()

 462    def index(self, point: PointType, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> int:
 463        """Return the index of the given point.
 464
 465        Args:
 466            point: Vertex to locate in transformed coordinates.
 467            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['abs_tol']``.
 468
 469        Returns:
 470            int: The index of the point.
 471
 472        Examples:
 473            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 474            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 475            >>> int(rect.index((0, 0)))
 476            0
 477        """
 478        point = tuple(point[:2])
 479
 480        if abs_tol is None:
 481            abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
 482        ind = np.where(
 483            (np.isclose(self.vertices, point, atol=abs_tol)).all(axis=1)
 484        )[0][0]
 485
 486        return ind
 487
 488    def remove(self, point: PointType) -> Self:
 489        """Remove a point from the shape.
 490
 491        Args:
 492            point (PointType): The point to remove.
 493
 494        Examples:
 495            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 496            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0)])
 497            >>> line.remove((0, 0))
 498            Shape(((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 499            >>> line.vertices
 500            ((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0))
 501        """
 502        ind = self.vertices.index(point)
 503        self.primary_points.pop(ind)
 504        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 505
 506        return self
 507
 508    def append(self, point: PointType) -> Self:
 509        """Append a point to the shape.
 510
 511        Args:
 512            point (PointType): The point to append.
 513
 514        Examples:
 515            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 516            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0)])
 517            >>> line.append((40, 0))
 518            >>> line.vertices
 519            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 520        """
 521        point = homogenize([point]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 522        self.primary_points.append(tuple(point[0][:2]))
 523        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 524        return self
 525
 526    def insert(self, index: int, point: PointType) -> Self:
 527        """Insert a point at a given index.
 528
 529        Args:
 530            index (int): The index to insert the point at.
 531            point (PointType): The point to insert.
 532
 533        Examples:
 534            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 535            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0)])
 536            >>> line.insert(1, (40, 0))
 537            Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 538        """
 539        point = homogenize([point]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 540        self.primary_points.insert(index, tuple(point[0][:2]))
 541        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 542
 543        return self
 544
 545    def extend(self, points: Sequence[PointType]) -> Self:
 546        """Extend the shape with a list of points.
 547
 548        Args:
 549            values (list[PointType]): The points to extend the shape with.
 550
 551        Examples:
 552            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 553            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0)])
 554            >>> line.extend([(40, 0), (80, 0)])
 555            Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 556        """
 557        homogenized = homogenize(points) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 558        self.primary_points.extend([tuple(x[:2]) for x in homogenized])
 559        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 560
 561        return self
 562
 563    def pop(self, index: int = -1) -> PointType:
 564        """Pop a point from the shape.
 565
 566        Args:
 567            index (int, optional): The index to pop the point from, defaults to -1.
 568
 569        Returns:
 570            PointType: The popped point.
 571
 572        Examples:
 573            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 574            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
 575            >>> line.pop()
 576            (40.0, 0.0)
 577            >>> line.vertices
 578            ((0.0, 0.0),)
 579        """
 580        point = self.vertices[index]
 581        self.primary_points.pop(index)
 582        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 583
 584        return point

 594    def _update(
 595        self,
 596        xform_matrix: array,
 597        reps: int = 0,
 598        take: slice | None = None,
 599        incr: float
 600        | tuple[float, float]
 601        | tuple[callable, Any]
 602        | tuple[InPlace, Any]
 603        | NDArray
 604        | Sequence[Sequence[float]]
 605        | None = None,
 606        dyn_ref: Callable | None = None,
 607        merge: bool = False,
 608        xform_type: TransformationType = None,
 609    ) -> Shape | Group:
 610        """Used internally. Update the shape with a transformation matrix.
 611
 612        Args:
 613            xform_matrix (array): The transformation matrix.
 614            reps (int, optional): The number of repetitions, defaults to 0.
 615            dyn_ref: Matrix factory built by the transform method when
 616                dynamic references are in use. Defaults to None.
 617
 618        Returns:
 619            Shape or Group: The updated shape or a group of shapes.
 620        """
 621        if reps == 0:
 622            fillet_radius = getattr(self, "fillet_radius", None)
 623            if fillet_radius:
 624                scale = max(decompose_transformations(xform_matrix)[2])
 625                self.fillet_radius = fillet_radius * scale
 626
 627            self.xform_matrix = self.xform_matrix @ xform_matrix
 628            self._clear_geometry_caches()
 629            res = self
 630        else:
 631            shapes = [self]
 632            shape = self
 633            if dyn_ref:
 634                pattern = Group()
 635                # Aliases shapes, so the pattern grows with the loop.
 636                pattern.elements = shapes
 637                targets = _Targets(self, pattern)
 638            else:
 639                targets = None
 640            for i in range(reps):
 641                shape = shape.copy()
 642                if targets is not None:
 643                    targets.active = shape
 644                xform_matrix = _next_xform_matrix(
 645                    xform_matrix, xform_type, incr, dyn_ref, targets, i
 646                )
 647                shape._update(xform_matrix)
 648                shapes.append(shape)
 649            res = Group(shapes)
 650
 651        if merge and reps > 0:
 652            merged = combine_shapes(res)
 653            for shape in merged:
 654                shape.copy_style(self)
 655            if len(merged) == 1:
 656                return merged[0]
 657            return merged
 658
 659        return res
 660
 661    def _translate_along_group(
 662        self, copies: Sequence[Shape], merge: bool
 663    ) -> Shape | Group:
 664        """Return a Group of this shape plus extra ``translate_along`` copies."""
 665        result = Group([self, *copies])
 666        if merge:
 667            return result.merge_shapes()
 668        return result
 669
 670    def __hash__(self) -> int:
 671        return hash(self.id)
 672
 673    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
 674        """Check if the shape is equal to another shape.
 675
 676        Args:
 677            other: Object to compare (must be a ``Shape`` with matching data).
 678
 679        Returns:
 680            bool: True if the shapes are equal, False otherwise.
 681        """
 682        if not hasattr(other, "type"):
 683            return False
 684        if other.type != Types.SHAPE:
 685            return False
 686
 687        len1 = len(self)
 688        len2 = len(other)
 689        if len1 == 0 and len2 == 0:
 690            res = True
 691        elif len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
 692            res = False
 693        elif isinstance(other, Shape) and len1 == len2:
 694            res = allclose(
 695                self.xform_matrix,
 696                other.xform_matrix,
 697                rtol=runtime_defaults["rel_tol"],
 698                atol=runtime_defaults["abs_tol"],
 699            ) and allclose(
 700                self.primary_points.nd_array,
 701                other.primary_points.nd_array,
 702                rtol=runtime_defaults["rel_tol"],
 703                atol=runtime_defaults["abs_tol"],
 704            )
 705        else:
 706            res = False
 707
 708        return res
 709
 710    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
 711        """Return whether the shape has any points.
 712
 713        Returns:
 714            bool: True if the shape has points, False otherwise.
 715        """
 716        return len(self.primary_points) > 0
 717
 718    def is_clockwise(self) -> bool:
 719        """Check if the shape is oriented clockwise.
 720
 721        Returns:
 722            bool: True if the shape is oriented clockwise, False otherwise.
 723
 724        Examples:
 725            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 726            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 727            >>> bool(rect.is_clockwise())
 728            False
 729        """
 730        if not self.closed:
 731            raise ValueError("Shape must be closed to check orientation")
 732        vertices = self.vertices
 733        area = polygon_area(vertices)
 734        return area < 0
 735
 736    def reordered(self, index: int) -> Self:
 737        """Return a copy of the shape starting from a point
 738        at the given index.
 739
 740        Args:
 741            index: Vertex index that becomes the new start (closed shapes only).
 742
 743        Returns:
 744            Shape: The shape with the starting point set.
 745
 746        Examples:
 747            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 748            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 749            >>> reordered = rect.reordered(1)
 750            >>> reordered.vertices
 751            ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0))
 752        """
 753        if not isinstance(index, int):
 754            raise TypeError("Index must be an integer")
 755        if not self.closed:
 756            raise ValueError("Shape must be closed to start from a point")
 757
 758        if index == 0:
 759            res = self.copy()
 760        else:
 761            shape = self.copy()
 762            vertices = shape.vertices
 763            shape[:] = vertices[index:] + vertices[:index]
 764            res = shape
 765
 766        return res
 767
 768    def lerp(self, edge: int, t: float) -> PointType:
 769        """Given an edge index and t value (between 0 and 1)
 770        returns the corresponding interpolated point.
 771
 772        Examples:
 773            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 774            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 775            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.lerp(0, 0.5)[:2])
 776            (20.0, 0.0)
 777        """
 778        return lerp_point(*self.edges[edge], t)

 780    def merge_collinears(self) -> Shape:
 781        """Merge collinear edges into a single polyline.
 782
 783        Examples:
 784            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 785            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (40, 0)])
 786            >>> merged = line.merge_collinears()
 787            >>> merged.vertices
 788            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 789        """
 790        return Group([self]).merge_shapes()[0]
 791
 792    def merge(
 793        self,
 794        other: Shape,
 795        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 796        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 797    ) -> Shape:
 798        """Return a new polyline by joining ``other`` after this shape.
 799
 800        Both shapes must be open. ``self[-1]`` must meet ``other[0]``
 801        within ``abs_tol``. The duplicated join vertex is dropped. If
 802        the joining edges are collinear, the join vertex is removed as
 803        well. Inputs are not mutated. Use ``connect`` to append in place.
 804
 805        Args:
 806            other: Open polyline whose first vertex meets this shape's last.
 807            rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 808            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 809
 810        Returns:
 811            Shape: A new open polyline.
 812
 813        Raises:
 814            ValueError: If either shape is closed, either has fewer than
 815                two vertices, or the endpoints do not meet.
 816
 817        Examples:
 818            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 819            >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
 820            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
 821            >>> a.merge(b).vertices
 822            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 823            >>> c = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (20, 80)])
 824            >>> a.merge(c).vertices
 825            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))
 826        """
 827        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 828        if self.closed or other.closed:
 829            raise ValueError("Only open polylines can be merged")
 830        if len(self) < 2 or len(other) < 2:
 831            raise ValueError("Both shapes must have at least two vertices")
 832        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 833        if not close_points_square(self[-1], other[0], dist2=abs_tol2):
 834            raise ValueError("Shapes are not connected: self[-1] must equal other[0]")
 835        verts1 = self.as_list()
 836        verts2 = other.as_list()
 837        if collinear_segments(
 838            self.edges[-1], other.edges[0], rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
 839        ):
 840            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2[1:]
 841        else:
 842            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2
 843
 844        return Shape(vertices, closed=False)
 845
 846    def connect(self, other: Shape) -> Self:
 847        """Connect two shapes by adding the other shape's vertices to self.
 848
 849        Args:
 850            other: Shape whose vertices are appended.
 851
 852        Examples:
 853            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 854            >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
 855            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
 856            >>> a.connect(b)
 857            Shape([(0.0, 0.0), ..., (40.0, 0.0)])
 858            >>> a.vertices
 859            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 860        """
 861        self.extend(other.vertices)
 862
 863        return self
 864
 865    def _chain_vertices(
 866        self,
 867        verts1: Sequence[PointType],
 868        verts2: Sequence[PointType],
 869        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 870        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 871    ) -> list[PointType] | None:
 872        """Chain two sets of vertices if they are connected.
 873
 874        Args:
 875            verts1 (list[PointType]): The first set of vertices.
 876            verts2 (list[PointType]): The second set of vertices.
 877            rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 878            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 879
 880        Returns:
 881            list[PointType] or None: The chained vertices or None if the vertices cannot be chained.
 882        """
 883        _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 884        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 885        start1, end1 = verts1[0], verts1[-1]
 886        start2, end2 = verts2[0], verts2[-1]
 887        same_starts = close_points_square(start1, start2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 888        same_ends = close_points_square(end1, end2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 889        if same_starts and same_ends:
 890            res = verts1
 891        elif close_points_square(end1, start2, dist2=abs_tol2):
 892            verts2.pop(0)
 893        elif close_points_square(start1, end2, dist2=abs_tol2):
 894            verts2.reverse()
 895            verts1.reverse()
 896            verts2.pop(0)
 897        elif same_starts:
 898            verts2.reverse()
 899            verts2.pop(-1)
 900            start = verts2[:]
 901            end = verts1[:]
 902            verts1 = start
 903            verts2 = end
 904        elif same_ends:
 905            verts2.reverse()
 906            verts2.pop(0)
 907        else:
 908            return None
 909        if same_starts and same_ends:
 910            all_verts = verts1 + verts2
 911            if not right_handed(all_verts):
 912                all_verts.reverse()
 913            res = all_verts
 914        else:
 915            res = verts1 + verts2
 916
 917        return res
 918
 919    def _is_polygon(self, vertices: Sequence[PointType]) -> bool:
 920        """Return True if the vertices form a polygon.
 921
 922        Args:
 923            vertices (list[PointType]): The vertices to check.
 924
 925        Returns:
 926            bool: True if the vertices form a polygon, False otherwise.
 927        """
 928        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
 929        return close_points_square(
 930            vertices[0][:2], vertices[-1][:2], dist2=abs_tol2
 931        )
 932
 933    def as_array(self, homogeneous: bool = False) -> NDArray:
 934        """Return the vertices as an array.
 935
 936        Args:
 937            homogeneous: If True, return homogeneous ``final_coords``.
 938
 939        Returns:
 940            ndarray: The vertices as an array.
 941
 942        Examples:
 943            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 944            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 945            >>> [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in rect.as_array()]
 946            [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
 947        """
 948        if homogeneous:
 949            # Use cached final_coords to avoid redundant matrix multiplication
 950            res = self.final_coords
 951        else:
 952            res = array(self.vertices)
 953        return res
 954
 955    def as_list(self) -> list[PointType]:
 956        """Return the vertices as a list of tuples.
 957
 958        Returns:
 959            list[tuple]: The vertices as a list of tuples.
 960
 961        Examples:
 962            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 963            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
 964            >>> line.as_list()
 965            [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 966        """

 969    @property
 970    def final_coords(self) -> NDArray:
 971        """The final coordinates of the shape. primary_points @ xform_matrix.
 972
 973        Returns:
 974            ndarray: The final coordinates of the shape.
 975
 976        Examples:
 977            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 978            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 979            >>> [(float(x), float(y), float(w)) for x, y, w in rect.final_coords]
 980            [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 40.0, 1.0), (0.0, 40.0, 1.0)]
 981        """
 982        if self.primary_points:
 983            # Cache the expensive matrix multiplication
 984            if (
 985                "_final_coords" not in self.__dict__
 986                or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
 987            ):
 988                self._final_coords = (
 989                    self.primary_points.homogen_coords @ self.xform_matrix
 990                )
 991            res = self._final_coords
 992        else:
 993            res = array([])
 994
 995        return res

 997    @property
 998    def angle(self) -> float:
 999        """Orientation angle of the shape (radians).
1000
1001        Examples:
1002            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1003            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1004            >>> float(line.angle)
1005            0.0
1006        """
1007        res = decompose_transformations(self.xform_matrix)[1]
1008        return positive_angle(res)

1010    @property
1011    def orientation(self) -> float:
1012        """Orientation angle of the shape (alias of ``angle``).
1013
1014        Examples:
1015            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1016            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1017            >>> float(line.orientation)
1018            0.0
1019        """
1020        return self.angle
1021
1022    @property
1023    def vertices(self) -> tuple[PointType]:
1024        """The final coordinates of the shape.
1025
1026        Returns:
1027            tuple: The final coordinates of the shape.
1028
1029        Examples:
1030            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1031            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1032            >>> rect.vertices
1033            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
1034        """
1035
1036        if self.primary_points:
1037            # Cache vertices computation and only recompute when data changes
1038            if (
1039                "_vertices" not in self.__dict__
1040                or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1041            ):
1042                res = tuple((x[0], x[1]) for x in (self.final_coords[:, :2]))
1043                self._vertices = res
1044                self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = False
1045            else:
1046                res = self._vertices
1047        else:
1048            res = ()
1049
1050        return res
1051
1052    @property
1053    def edge_lengths(self) -> list[float]:
1054        """Return the lengths of the shape edges.
1055
1056        For closed shapes, the closing edge from the last vertex back to the
1057        first is included.
1058
1059        Returns:
1060            list[float]: Edge lengths in vertex order.
1061
1062        Examples:
1063            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1064            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (30, 40), (60, 40)])
1065            >>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in line.edge_lengths]
1066            [50.0, 30.0]
1067            >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (3, 0), (3, 4)], closed=True)
1068            >>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in tri.edge_lengths]
1069            [3.0, 4.0, 5.0]
1070        """
1071        if not self.primary_points:
1072            return []
1073        if (
1074            "_edge_lengths" not in self.__dict__
1075            or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1076        ):
1077            self._edge_lengths = tuple(
1078                distance(*edge) for edge in self.edges
1079            )
1080        return list(self._edge_lengths)
1081
1082    @property
1083    def vertex_pairs(self) -> list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]:
1084        """Return a list of connected pairs of vertices.
1085
1086        Returns:
1087            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of connected pairs of vertices.
1088
1089        Examples:
1090            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1091            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1092            >>> rect.vertex_pairs
1093            [((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0))]
1094        """
1095        vertices = list(self.vertices)
1096        if self.closed:
1097            vertices.append(vertices[0])
1098        return connected_pairs(vertices)
1099
1100    @property
1101    def orig_coords(self) -> NDArray:
1102        """The primary points in homogeneous coordinates.
1103
1104        Returns:
1105            ndarray: The primary points in homogeneous coordinates.
1106
1107        Examples:
1108            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1109            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1110            >>> [(float(x), float(y), float(w)) for x, y, w in rect.orig_coords]
1111            [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 40.0, 1.0), (0.0, 40.0, 1.0)]
1112        """
1113        return self.primary_points.homogen_coords

1115    @property
1116    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
1117        """Return the bounding box of the shape.
1118
1119        Returns:
1120            BoundingBox: The bounding box of the shape.
1121
1122        Examples:
1123            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1124            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1125            >>> float(rect.b_box.width)
1126            40.0
1127        """
1128        if self.primary_points:
1129            self._b_box = bounding_box(self.final_coords)
1130        else:
1131            self._b_box = bounding_box([(0, 0)])
1132        return self._b_box
1133
1134    @property
1135    def area(self) -> float:
1136        """Return the area of the shape.
1137
1138        Returns:
1139            float: The area of the shape.
1140
1141        Examples:
1142            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1143            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1144            >>> float(rect.area)
1145            1600.0
1146        """
1147        if self.closed:
1148            vertices = self.vertices[:]
1149            abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1150            if not close_points_square(
1151                vertices[0], vertices[-1], dist2=abs_tol2
1152            ):
1153                vertices = list(vertices) + [vertices[0]]
1154            res = polygon_area(vertices)
1155        else:
1156            res = 0
1157
1158        return res
1159
1160    @property
1161    def total_length(self) -> float:
1162        """Return the total length of the shape.
1163
1164        Returns:
1165            float: The total length of the shape.
1166
1167        Examples:
1168            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1169            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
1170            >>> line.total_length
1171            80.0
1172            >>> line2 = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
1173            >>> round(float(line2.total_length), 6)
1174            136.568542
1175        """
1176        if not self.primary_points:
1177            return 0.0
1178        if (
1179            "_total_length" not in self.__dict__
1180            or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1181        ):
1182            self._total_length = float(sum(self.edge_lengths))
1183        return self._total_length
1184
1185    @property
1186    def is_polygon(self) -> bool:
1187        """Return True if 'closed'.
1188
1189        Returns:
1190            bool: True if the shape is closed, False otherwise.
1191
1192        Examples:
1193            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1194            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1195            >>> rect.is_polygon
1196            True
1197        """
1198        return self.closed
1199
1200    def clear(self) -> Self:
1201        """Clear all points and reset the style attributes.
1202
1203        Returns:
1204            None
1205
1206        Examples:
1207            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1208            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1209            >>> rect.clear()
1210            Shape()
1211            >>> rect.vertices
1212            ()
1213        """
1214        self.primary_points = Points()
1215        self.xform_matrix = identity_matrix()
1216        self._b_box = None
1217        self._clear_geometry_caches()
1218
1219        return self
1220
1221    def count(self, point: PointType) -> int:
1222        """Return the number of times the point is found in the shape.
1223
1224        Args:
1225            point (PointType): The point to count.
1226
1227        Returns:
1228            int: The number of times the point is found in the shape.
1229
1230        Examples:
1231            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1232            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1233            >>> rect.count((0, 0))
1234            1
1235        """
1236        verts = self.orig_coords @ self.xform_matrix
1237        verts = verts[:, :2]
1238        n = verts.shape[0]
1239        point = array(point[:2])
1240        values = np.tile(point, (n, 1))
1241        col1 = (verts[:, 0] - values[:, 0]) ** 2
1242        col2 = (verts[:, 1] - values[:, 1]) ** 2
1243        distances = col1 + col2
1244        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1245
1246        return np.count_nonzero(distances <= abs_tol2)
1247
1248    def copy(self) -> Shape:
1249        """Return a copy of the shape.
1250
1251        Returns:
1252            Shape: A copy of the shape.
1253
1254        Examples:
1255            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1256            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1257            >>> copy = rect.copy()
1258            >>> copy == rect
1259            True
1260            >>> copy is rect
1261            False
1262        """
1263        self._b_box = None
1264        return deepcopy(self)
1265
1266    def segment(
1267        self, i: int, j: int, midpoints: bool = False
1268    ) -> tuple[PointType]:
1269        """Returns a line segment with shape[i] and shape[j] endpoints.
1270        If midpoints is True then returns a line segment between midpoints
1271        of the shape.edges[i] and shape.edges[j]
1272
1273        Examples:
1274            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1275            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1276            >>> p0, p1 = rect.segment(0, 2)
1277            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p0[:2])
1278            (0.0, 0.0)
1279            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p1[:2])
1280            (40.0, 40.0)
1281        """
1282        if midpoints:
1283            res = (self.edge_midpoint(i), self.edge_midpoint(j))
1284        else:
1285            res = (self[i], self[j])
1286
1287        return res
1288
1289    def edge_midpoint(self, i: int) -> PointType:
1290        """Return the midpoint of shape.edges[i].
1291
1292        Examples:
1293            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1294            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1295            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.edge_midpoint(0)[:2])
1296            (20.0, 0.0)
1297        """
1298
1299        n = len(self)
1300        edge = (self[i], self[(i + 1) % n])
1301
1302        return midpoint(*edge)
1303
1304    @property
1305    def edge_midpoints(self) -> list[PointType]:
1306        """Return a list of the edge midpoints.
1307
1308        Examples:
1309            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1310            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1311            >>> rect.edge_midpoints
1312            [(20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0), (20.0, 40.0), (0.0, 20.0)]
1313        """
1314        edges = self.edges
1315
1316        return [midpoint(*edge) for edge in edges]
1317
1318    @property
1319    def edges(self) -> list[LineType]:
1320        """Return a list of the edges of the shape.
1321
1322        Edges are represented as tuples of points:
1323        edge: ((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
1324        edges: [((x1, y1), (x2, y2)), ((x2, y2), (x3, y3)), ...]
1325
1326        Returns:
1327            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of edges.
1328
1329        Examples:
1330            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1331            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1332            >>> rect.edges
1333            (((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1334        """
1335        vertices = list(self.vertices[:])
1336        if self.closed:
1337            vertices.append(vertices[0])
1338
1339        return tuple(connected_pairs(vertices))
1340
1341    @property
1342    def midpoints(self) -> list[PointType]:
1343        """Returns a list of the midpoints of the edges.
1344
1345        Examples:
1346            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1347            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1348            >>> rect.midpoints
1349            [(20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0), (20.0, 40.0), (0.0, 20.0)]
1350        """
1351        return [midpoint(*edge) for edge in self.edges]
1352
1353    @property
1354    def segments(self) -> list[LineType]:
1355        """Return a list of edges.
1356
1357        Edges are represented as tuples of points:
1358        edge: ((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
1359        edges: [((x1, y1), (x2, y2)), ((x2, y2), (x3, y3)), ...]
1360
1361        Returns:
1362            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of edges.
1363
1364        Examples:
1365            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1366            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1367            >>> rect.segments
1368            (((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1369        """
1370
1371        return self.edges
1372
1373    def reverse(self) -> Self:
1374        """Reverse the order of the vertices.
1375
1376        Returns:
1377            None
1378
1379        Examples:
1380            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1381            >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
1382            >>> tri.reverse()
1383            Shape(((40.0, 40.0), (40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1384            >>> tri.vertices
1385            ((40.0, 40.0), (40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0))
1386        """
1387        self.primary_points.reverse()
1388        self._clear_geometry_caches()
1389
1390        return self

1466    @property
1467    def midpoint(self) -> PointType:
1468        """Center of the axis-aligned bounding box.
1469
1470        Examples:
1471            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1472            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1473            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.midpoint[:2])
1474            (20.0, 20.0)
1475        """
1476        x1, y1 = self.southwest
1477        x2, y2 = self.northeast
1478
1479        xc = (x1 + x2) / 2
1480        yc = (y1 + y2) / 2
1481
1482        return (xc, yc)

1712    def get_inflated_b_box(
1713        self,
1714        left_margin: float | None = None,
1715        bottom_margin: float | None = None,
1716        right_margin: float | None = None,
1717        top_margin: float | None = None,
1718    ) -> BoundingBox:
1719        """Return a bounding box expanded by the given margins.
1720
1721        Args:
1722            left_margin: Outward offset on the left; other margins default from it.
1723            bottom_margin: Outward offset on the bottom.
1724            right_margin: Outward offset on the right.
1725            top_margin: Outward offset on the top.
1726
1727        Returns:
1728            Inflated ``BoundingBox``.
1729
1730        Examples:
1731            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1732            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1733            >>> inflated = rect.get_inflated_b_box(1)
1734            >>> inflated.corners
1735            ((-1.0, 41.0), (-1.0, -1.0), (41.0, -1.0), (41.0, 41.0))
1736        """
1737
1738        if bottom_margin is None:
1739            bottom_margin = left_margin
1740        if right_margin is None:
1741            right_margin = left_margin
1742        if top_margin is None:
1743            top_margin = bottom_margin
1744
1745        x, y = self.southwest[:2]
1746        southwest = (x - left_margin, y - bottom_margin)
1747
1748        x, y = self.northeast[:2]
1749        northeast = (x + right_margin, y + top_margin)
1750
1751        return BoundingBox(southwest, northeast)
1752
1753    def offset_line(
1754        self, side: Side | str, offset: float
1755    ) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
1756        """Offset a bounding-box edge outward (negative ``offset`` goes inward).
1757
1758        Args:
1759            side: ``Side`` enum member or name accepted by ``BoundingBox``.
1760            offset: Perpendicular offset distance.
1761
1762        Returns:
1763            Offset segment as two points.
1764
1765        Examples:
1766            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1767            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1768            >>> rect.offset_line('left', 1)
1769            ((-1.0, 0.0), (-1.0, 40.0))
1770        """
1771        return self.b_box.offset_line(side, offset)
1772
1773    def offset_point(
1774        self, anchor: Anchor | str, dx: float, dy: float
1775    ) -> PointType:
1776        """Return a point offset from a bounding-box anchor.
1777
1778        Args:
1779            anchor: ``Anchor`` enum member or alias.
1780            dx: Horizontal offset.
1781            dy: Vertical offset.
1782
1783        Returns:
1784            Offset point in canvas coordinates.
1785
1786        Examples:
1787            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1788            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1789            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.offset_point('midpoint', 20, 0)[:2])
1790            (40.0, 20.0)
1791        """
1792        return self.b_box.offset_point(anchor, dx, dy)
1793
1794    def centered(
1795        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1796    ) -> PointType:
1797        """
1798        Get the center of the reference item.
1799
1800        Args:
1801            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1802            dx (float): The x offset.
1803            dy (float): The y offset.
1804
1805        Returns:
1806            PointType: The item.midpoint of the reference item's bounding-box.
1807
1808        Examples:
1809            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1810            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1811            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1812            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.centered(ref)[:2])
1813            (20.0, 20.0)
1814        """
1815
1816        x, y = item.midpoint[:2]
1817        x += dx
1818        y += dy
1819        return x, y
1820
1821    def left_of(
1822        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1823    ) -> PointType:
1824        """
1825        Get the item.west of the reference item.
1826
1827        Args:
1828            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1829            dx (float): The x offset.
1830            dy (float): The y offset.
1831
1832        Returns:
1833            PointType: The item.west of the reference item's bounding-box.
1834
1835        Examples:
1836            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1837            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1838            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1839            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.left_of(ref)[:2])
1840            (-40.0, 20.0)
1841        """
1842        x, y = item.west[:2]
1843        w2 = self.width / 2
1844        x += dx - w2
1845        y += dy
1846        return x, y
1847
1848    def right_of(
1849        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1850    ) -> PointType:
1851        """
1852        Get the item.east of the reference item.
1853
1854        Args:
1855            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1856            dx (float): The x offset.
1857            dy (float): The y offset.
1858
1859        Returns:
1860            PointType: The item.east of the reference item's bounding-box.
1861
1862        Examples:
1863            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1864            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1865            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1866            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.right_of(ref)[:2])
1867            (80.0, 20.0)
1868        """
1869        x, y = item.east[:2]
1870        w2 = self.width / 2
1871        x += dx + w2
1872        y += dy
1873        return x, y
1874
1875    def above(
1876        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1877    ) -> PointType:
1878        """
1879        Get the item.north of the reference item.
1880
1881        Args:
1882            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1883            dx (float): The x offset.
1884            dy (float): The y offset.
1885
1886        Returns:
1887            PointType: The item.north of the reference item's bounding-box.
1888
1889        Examples:
1890            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1891            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1892            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1893            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.above(ref)[:2])
1894            (20.0, 80.0)
1895        """
1896        x, y = item.north[:2]
1897        h2 = self.height / 2
1898        x += dx
1899        y += dy + h2
1900        return x, y

1903        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0

1929    def above_left(
1930        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1931    ) -> PointType:
1932        """
1933        Get the item.northwest of the reference item.
1934
1935        Args:
1936            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1937            dx (float): The x offset.
1938            dy (float): The y offset.
1939
1940        Returns:
1941            PointType: The item.northwest of the reference item's bounding-box.
1942
1943        Examples:
1944            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg

1947            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.above_left(ref)[:2])
1948            (-40.0, 80.0)

1950        x, y = item.northwest[:]

1952        h2 = self.height / 2
1953        x += dx - w2
1954        y += dy + h2

2045    def polar_pos(
2046        self, item: Shape | Group, angle: float, radius: float
2047    ) -> PointType:
2048        """
2049        Get the polar position of the reference item.
2050
2051        Args:
2052            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
2053            theta (float): The angle in radians.
2054            radius (float): The radius.
2055
2056        Returns:
2057            PointType: The polar position of the reference item.
2058
2059        Examples:
2060            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2061            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2062            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
2063            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.polar_pos(ref, 0, 5)[:2])
2064            (25.0, 20.0)
2065        """
2066
2067        x, y = item.midpoint[:2]
2068
2069        x1, y1 = polar_to_cartesian(radius, angle)
2070        x += x1
2071        y += y1
2072
2073        return x, y

2077    def reorder_vertices(
2078        self, value: PointType, index: int = 0, tol: float | None = None
2079    ) -> Shape | None:
2080        """If index is not given, the vertex with the given value will be
2081        the first index.
2082        If index is given, the vertex with the given value will be
2083        at the given index.
2084        The rest of the indices will be shifted accordingly.
2085
2086        Shape must be closed.
2087
2088        Args:
2089            index (int): The target index.
2090            value (PointType): The vertex to relocate at the given index.
2091
2092        Returns:
2093            Shape: A new shape with the adjusted vertices.
2094
2095        Examples:
2096            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2097            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2098            >>> reordered = rect.reorder_vertices((40, 40))
2099            >>> reordered.vertices
2100            ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
2101        """
2102
2103        if not isinstance(value, Sequence) or len(value) < 2:
2104            raise TypeError("Value must be a [x, y] sequence")
2105
2106        if self.closed:
2107            vertices = list(self.vertices)
2108            if value in vertices:
2109                cur_index = vertices.index(value)
2110            else:
2111                if tol is None:
2112                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2113                dist, ind = min(
2114                    [(distance(value, v), i) for i, v in enumerate(vertices)],
2115                    key=lambda x: x[0],
2116                )
2117                if dist < tol:
2118                    cur_index = ind
2119                else:
2120                    return None
2121
2122            shift = index - cur_index
2123            if shift == 0:
2124                return None
2125
2126            if value in vertices:
2127                new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2128            else:
2129                if tol is None:
2130                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2131                if distance(value, vertices[cur_index]) < tol:
2132                    new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2133                else:
2134                    new_vertices = None
2135            if new_vertices is not None:
2136                res = self.copy()
2137                res[:] = new_vertices
2138            else:
2139                res = None
2140        else:
2141            res = None
2142
2143        return res
2144
2145
2146def trim_margins(
2147    item: Shape | Group,
2148    left: float = 0,
2149    bottom: float = 0,
2150    right: float = 0,
2151    top: float = 0,
2152) -> Shape | Group:
2153    """Trim the margins of a Shape or Group.
2154
2155    Args:
2156        item (Shape | Group): The Shape or Group to trim.
2157        left (float, optional): The left margin to trim. Defaults to 0.
2158        bottom (float, optional): The bottom margin to trim. Defaults to 0.
2159        right (float, optional): The right margin to trim. Defaults to 0.
2160        top (float, optional): The top margin to trim. Defaults to 0.
2161
2162    Returns:
2163        Shape | Group: The trimmed Shape or Group.
2164
2165    Examples:
2166        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2167        >>> trimmed = trim_margins(square)
2168        >>> trimmed
2169        Group()
2170    """
2171    corners = item.b_box.get_inflated_b_box(
2172        -left, -bottom, -right, -top
2173    ).corners
2174    clipper = Shape(corners, closed=True)
2175
2176    return clip(item, clipper, exclude_clipper=True)
2177
2178
2179def clip(
2180    item: Shape | Group,
2181    clipper: Shape,
2182    exclude_clipper: bool = False,
2183    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2184    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2185    merge: bool = True,
2186) -> Shape | Group:
2187    """Clip a Shape or Group against a closed clipper polygon.
2188
2189    Args:
2190        item: Shape or Group to clip.
2191        clipper: Closed clipping region.
2192        exclude_clipper: If True, treat clipper boundary specially in tests.
2193        rel_tol: Relative intersection tolerance.
2194        abs_tol: Absolute intersection tolerance.
2195        merge: If True, merge clipped fragments via ``merge_shapes``.
2196
2197    Returns:
2198        Shape | Group: Clipped geometry with style copied from ``item``.
2199
2200    Raises:
2201        TypeError: If ``item`` is neither Shape nor Group.
2202
2203    Examples:
2204        >>> subject = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2205        >>> window = sg.Shape([(20, 20), (60, 20), (60, 60), (20, 60)], closed=True)
2206        >>> clip(subject, window)  # doctest: +SKIP
2207    """
2208    if isinstance(item, Group):
2209        return _clip_group(item, clipper, exclude_clipper, rel_tol, abs_tol)
2210    elif isinstance(item, Shape):
2211        clipped_item = _clip_shape(
2212            item,
2213            clipper,
2214            exclude_clipper,
2215            rel_tol,
2216            abs_tol,
2217        )
2218        if clipped_item.type == Types.GROUP:
2219            for clipped_shape in clipped_item:
2220                clipped_shape.copy_style(item)
2221        else:
2222            clipped_item.copy_style(item)
2223
2224        if merge:
2225            clipped_item = clipped_item.merge_shapes()
2226
2227        return clipped_item
2228
2229
2230def _clip_group(
2231    group: Group,
2232    clipper: Shape,
2233    exclude_clipper: bool = True,
2234    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2235    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2236) -> Group:
2237    """Clip each element of ``group`` against ``clipper`` and collect results."""
2238    res = Group()
2239
2240    for item in group.elements:
2241        if item.type == Types.GROUP:
2242            clipped_item = _clip_group(
2243                item,
2244                clipper,
2245                exclude_clipper,
2246                rel_tol,
2247                abs_tol,
2248            )
2249        elif item.type == Types.SHAPE:
2250            clipped_item = _clip_shape(
2251                item,
2252                clipper,
2253                exclude_clipper,
2254                rel_tol,
2255                abs_tol,
2256            )
2257            if clipped_item.type == Types.GROUP:
2258                for clipped_shape in clipped_item:
2259                    clipped_shape.copy_style(item)
2260            else:
2261                clipped_item.copy_style(item)
2262        else:
2263            raise TypeError("Invalid item type")
2264
2265        if clipped_item.type == Types.GROUP:
2266            if len(clipped_item) > 0:
2267                res.append(clipped_item)
2268        else:
2269            res.append(clipped_item)
2270
2271    return res
2272
2273
2274def _clip_shape(
2275    shape: Shape,
2276    clipper: Shape,
2277    exclude_clipper: bool = False,
2278    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2279    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2280) -> Shape | Group:
2281    """Clip a single shape to the interior of ``clipper``."""
2282    if not clipper.closed:
2283        raise ValueError("Clipper shape is not closed")
2284    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
2285    n_shape = len(shape)
2286    segments = [[p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in shape.edges] + [
2287        [p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in clipper.edges
2288    ]
2289    intersections = all_intersections(segments)
2290
2291    split_points_by_index = {}
2292    for key, value in intersections[0].items():
2293        points = [point_data[0] for point_data in value]
2294        split_points_by_index[key] = remove_duplicate_points(points)
2295
2296    def split_segment(segment_index: int) -> list[LineType]:
2297        points = split_points_by_index.get(segment_index, [])
2298        if points:
2299            return multi_split_segment(segments[segment_index], points)
2300        return [segments[segment_index]]
2301
2302    clipped = Group()
2303    shape_vertices = shape.vertices
2304    clipper_vertices = clipper.vertices
2305    if shape.closed:
2306        shape_segment_count = n_shape
2307    else:
2308        shape_segment_count = n_shape - 1
2309
2310    for segment_index in range(shape_segment_count):
2311        for seg in split_segment(segment_index):
2312            if not isclose(
2313                distance(*seg), 0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
2314            ) and in_polygon(midpoint(*seg), clipper_vertices, exclude_clipper):
2315                clipped.append(Shape(seg))
2316
2317    if shape.closed and not exclude_clipper:
2318        for segment_index in range(shape_segment_count, len(segments)):
2319            for seg in split_segment(segment_index):
2320                if not isclose(
2321                    distance(*seg),
2322                    0,
2323                    rel_tol=rel_tol,
2324                    abs_tol=abs_tol,
2325                ) and in_polygon(
2326                    midpoint(*seg),
2327                    shape_vertices,
2328                    exclude_clipper,
2329                ):
2330                    clipped.append(Shape(seg))
2331
2332    if len(clipped) == 1:
2333        return clipped[0]
2334
2335    return clipped
2336
2337
2338def custom_attributes(item: Shape) -> list[str]:
2339    """Return a list of custom attributes of a Shape or Group instance.
2340
2341    Args:
2342        item (Shape): The Shape or Group instanc
2343    Returns:
2344        list[str]: A list of custom attribute names.
2345
2346    Examples:
2347        >>> poly = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
2348        >>> 'closed' not in custom_attributes(poly)
2349        True
2350    """
2351    dummy = Shape([(0, 0), (1, 0)])
2352    native_attribs = set(dir(dummy))
2353    known_shape_attribs = set(shape_attributes)
2354    custom_attribs = set(dir(item)) - native_attribs - known_shape_attribs
2355
2356    if hasattr(item, "_aliases") and isinstance(item._aliases, dict):
2357        custom_attribs = custom_attribs.difference(set(item._aliases.keys()))
2358
2359    return sorted(custom_attribs)
2360
2361
2362@dataclass
2363class Clipping:
2364    """Pair of a draw target and a clipper shape.
2365
2366    Attributes:
2367        target: Shape or Group to be clipped.
2368        clipper: Closed Shape used as the clipping region.
2369        type: Always ``Types.CLIPPING``.
2370
2371    Examples:
2372        >>> subject = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
2373        >>> window = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2374        >>> pair = Clipping(subject, window)
2375        >>> pair.target.vertices
2376        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0))
2377        >>> pair.clipper.vertices
2378        ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 20.0), (0.0, 20.0))
2379    """
2380
2381    target: Shape | Group
2382    clipper: Shape
2383
2384    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
2385        self.type = Types.CLIPPING
2386        self.subtype = Types.CLIPPING
2387
2388    def __repr__(self) -> str:
2389        """Return a Clipping string from the target and clipper.
2390
2391        Examples:
2392            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2393            >>> pair = sg.Clipping(
2394            ...     sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)]),
2395            ...     sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (0, 40)], closed=True),
2396            ... )
2397            >>> repr(pair)
2398            'Clipping(target=Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))), clipper=Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 40.0))))'
2399        """
2400        return f"Clipping(target={self.target!r}, clipper={self.clipper!r})"
2401
2402
2403def polygon_diff(
2404    shape1: Shape,
2405    shape2: Shape,
2406    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2407    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2408    merge: bool = True,
2409) -> Group:
2410    """Return the difference of two closed polygons (``shape1 \\ shape2``).
2411
2412    Args:
2413        shape1: Shape to clip (must be closed).
2414        shape2: Clipping region (must be closed).
2415        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
2416        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2417        merge: If True, merge resulting edge fragments into shapes.
2418
2419    Returns:
2420        Group: Segments or merged shapes belonging to ``shape1`` outside
2421        ``shape2``.
2422
2423    Raises:
2424        Warning: If either shape is not closed (raised as ``Warning``).
2425
2426    Examples:
2427        >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2428        >>> b = sg.Shape([(40, 40), (30, 40), (30, 30), (40, 30)], closed=True)
2429        >>> polygon_diff(a, b)  # doctest: +SKIP
2430    """
2431    exclude_clipper = False
2432    if not (shape1.closed and shape2.closed):
2433        raise Warning("Both shapes must be closed")
2434
2435    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
2436    segments = [[p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in shape1.edges] + [
2437        [p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in shape2.edges
2438    ]
2439    intersections = all_intersections(segments, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
2440
2441    all_segments_ = []
2442    for key, value in intersections[0].items():
2443        segment = segments[key]
2444        points = [x[0] for x in value]
2445        points = remove_duplicate_points(points)
2446        all_segments_.append(multi_split_segment(segment, points))
2447
2448    diff_ = Group()
2449    shape_vertices = shape1.vertices
2450    shape2_vertices = shape2.vertices
2451    for segs in all_segments_:
2452        for seg in segs:
2453            in1 = in_polygon(midpoint(*seg), shape_vertices)
2454            in2 = in_polygon(
2455                midpoint(*seg), shape2_vertices, not exclude_clipper
2456            )
2457            if in1 and not in2:
2458                diff_.append(Shape(seg))
2459
2460    if merge:
2461        diff_ = diff_.merge_shapes()
2462
2463    return diff_
2464
2465
2466def polygon_difference(
2467    shape1: Shape,
2468    shape2: Shape,
2469    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2470    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2471    merge: bool = True,
2472) -> Group:
2473    """Alias for ``polygon_diff``.
2474
2475    Args:
2476        shape1: Shape to clip.
2477        shape2: Clipping region.
2478        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
2479        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2480        merge: If True, merge resulting fragments.
2481
2482    Returns:
2483        Group: Difference result.
2484
2485    Examples:
2486        >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2487        >>> b = sg.Shape([(40, 40), (30, 40), (30, 30), (40, 30)], closed=True)
2488        >>> polygon_difference(a, b)  # doctest: +SKIP
2489    """
2490    return polygon_diff(
2491        shape1, shape2, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol, merge=merge
2492    )
2493
2494
2495def polygon_intersection(
2496    shape1: Shape, shape2: Shape, merge: bool = True
2497) -> Shape | Group:
2498    """Return the intersection of two closed polygons.
2499
2500    Args:
2501        shape1: First closed shape.
2502        shape2: Second closed shape.
2503        merge: If True, merge resulting edge fragments.
2504
2505    Returns:
2506        Group: Intersection fragments or merged shapes.
2507
2508    Examples:
2509        >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2510        >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 20), (60, 20), (60, 60), (20, 60)], closed=True)
2511        >>> polygon_intersection(a, b)  # doctest: +SKIP
2512    """
2513    if not (shape1.closed and shape2.closed):
2514        raise ValueError("Invalid input: shape1 and shape2 must be closed!")
2515    return clip(shape1, shape2, merge=merge)
2516
2517
2518def polygon_xor(
2519    shape1: Shape,
2520    shape2: Shape,
2521    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2522    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2523    merge: bool = True,
2524) -> Group:
2525    """Return the symmetric difference of two closed polygons.
2526
2527    Args:
2528        shape1: First closed shape.
2529        shape2: Second closed shape.
2530        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
2531        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2532        merge: If True, merge the combined result.
2533
2534    Returns:
2535        Group: Symmetric difference fragments or merged shapes.
2536
2537    Examples:
2538        >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2539        >>> b = sg.Shape([(40, 40), (30, 40), (30, 30), (40, 30)], closed=True)
2540        >>> polygon_xor(a, b)  # doctest: +SKIP
2541    """
2542    res1 = polygon_diff(shape1, shape2, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
2543    res2 = polygon_diff(shape2, shape1, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
2544
2545    res = Group([res1, res2])
2546
2547    if merge:
2548        res = res.merge_shapes(rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
2549
2550    return res
2551
2552
2553def all_segments(
2554    item: Shape | Group,
2555    n_round: int = 1,
2556    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2557    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2558) -> list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]:
2559    """Collect unique line segments from a Shape or Group.
2560
2561    Args:
2562        item: Input shape or group.
2563        n_round: Decimal places used when rounding segment coordinates.
2564        rel_tol: Relative tolerance for segment comparison.
2565        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance for segment comparison.
2566
2567    Returns:
2568        list[LineType]: Deduplicated line segments.
2569
2570    Examples:
2571        >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (20, 80)], closed=True)
2572        >>> all_segments(tri)
2573        [((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((20.0, 80.0), (0.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))]
2574    """
2575
2576    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
2577    if isinstance(item, Group):
2578        shapes = item.all_shapes
2579    else:
2580        shapes = [item]
2581    edges = []
2582    for shp in shapes:
2583        edges.extend(shp.edges)
2584    segments = [[p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in edges]
2585    intersections = all_intersections(segments)
2586
2587    all_segments_ = []
2588    for key, value in intersections[0].items():
2589        segment = segments[key]
2590        points = [x[0] for x in value]
2591        points = remove_duplicate_points(points)
2592        all_segments_.append(multi_split_segment(segment, points))
2593
2594    edges = []
2595    for segs in all_segments_:
2596        for seg in segs:
2597            if distance(*seg) < 0.1:
2598                continue
2599            seg = around((seg), n_round)
2600            seg = (tuple(seg[0]), tuple(seg[1]))
2601            edges.append(seg)
2602
2603    return edges
2604
2605
2606def get_loop(
2607    edges: Sequence[LineType], start_edge: LineType, ccw: bool = True
2608) -> Shape:
2609    """Trace a closed loop through ``edges`` starting from ``start_edge``.
2610
2611    Args:
2612        edges: Segment graph to search.
2613        start_edge: Initial directed edge.
2614        ccw: If True, prefer counterclockwise turns at each node.
2615
2616    Returns:
2617        Closed ``Shape`` when a loop is found, otherwise an open polyline.
2618
2619    Examples:
2620        >>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (40, 40)), ((40, 40), (0, 0))]
2621        >>> loop = get_loop(edges, ((0, 0), (40, 0)))
2622        >>> loop.vertices
2623        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0))
2624        >>> loop.closed
2625        True
2626    """
2627    G = nx.Graph()
2628    G.add_edges_from(edges)
2629    if not ccw:
2630        start_edge = (start_edge[1], start_edge[0])
2631
2632    res = [*start_edge]
2633    start_node = start_edge[0]
2634    cur_node = start_edge[1]
2635    cur_edge = start_edge
2636    open_ = True
2637    while open_:
2638        edges_cur_node = set(G.edges(cur_node))
2639        angles = []
2640        for edge in edges_cur_node:
2641            if (edge[1], edge[0]) == cur_edge:
2642                continue
2643            if edge[1] == start_node:
2644                open_ = False
2645                break
2646            angle = angle_between_lines3(*cur_edge, edge[1])
2647            angle = positive_angle(angle)
2648            pi_ = round(pi, 2)
2649            if round(angle, 2) not in (0, -pi_, pi_, 2 * pi_):
2650                angles.append((angle, edge))
2651        if open_:
2652            angles.sort()
2653            if not angles:
2654                break
2655            cur_edge = angles[0][1]
2656            cur_node = cur_edge[1]
2657            res.append(cur_node)
2658
2659    return Shape(res, closed=not (open_))
2660
2661
2662def get_partition(
2663    item: Shape | Group, edge_index: int, ccw: bool = True
2664) -> Shape:
2665    """
2666    Get a sub-region from a shape or group object.
2667    Draw the segments by using canvas.draw_all_segments first to get the indices.
2668    Args:
2669        item Shape | Group: A shape or a group object.
2670        edge_index int: Index of the starting edge of the partition.
2671        ccw bool: If True, the region is formed by looping in
2672        counterclockwise direction, clockwise otherwise.
2673
2674    Returns:
2675        The resulting shape object.
2676
2677    Examples:
2678        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2679        >>> part = get_partition(square, 0)
2680        >>> part.vertices
2681        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
2682        >>> part.closed
2683        True
2684    """
2685
2686    edges = all_segments(item)
2687
2688    return get_loop(edges, edges[edge_index], ccw)
@dataclass
class Clipping:
