 107class Shape(Base, CommonStyle):
 108    """Polyline/polygon drawable with style and affine transform state.
 109
 110    Constructed from a sequence of points. When ``closed`` is True (or the
 111    first and last points coincide), the shape is treated as a polygon for
 112    fill and boolean operations.
 113    If the first and last points coincide then the last point is removed.
 114
 115    Omitted style arguments are stored from ``user_defaults`` at init.
 116    ``color`` and ``alpha`` stay unset unless passed. ``color`` sets both
 117    ``line_color`` and ``fill_color``. ``alpha`` sets both ``line_alpha``
 118    and ``fill_alpha``. Reading a ``line_color`` / ``fill_color`` /
 119    ``line_alpha`` / ``fill_alpha`` that was later set to ``None`` returns
 120    the matching configured default. Use sg.doc(sg.Shape) to see the defaults.
 121
 122    Style color/alpha properties and ``copy_style`` come from ``CommonStyle``.
 123
 124    Attributes:
 125        primary_points: ``Points`` storage.
 126        xform_matrix: 3×3 affine transform (row form).
 127        closed: Whether the outline is closed.
 128        fill / stroke: Draw fill and/or stroke.
 129        line_width / line_color / fill_color: Common style attributes.
 130        subtype: Shape subtype (``Types.SHAPE``, ``Types.CIRCLE``, …).
 131        id: Unique object id.
 132
 133    Examples:
 134        >>> s = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 135        >>> s.vertices
 136        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
 137        >>> s.width
 138        40.0
 139    """
 140
 141    __slots__ = [
 142        "_alpha",
 143        "_color",
 144        "_fill_alpha",
 145        "_fill_color",
 146        "_line_alpha",
 147        "_line_color",
 148        "back_style",
 149        "closed",
 150        "double_color",
 151        "double_distance",
 152        "draw_double",
 153        "draw_fillets",
 154        "draw_markers",
 155        "even_odd",
 156        "fill",
 157        "fill_mode",
 158        "fillet_radius",
 159        "gradient",
 160        "line_cap",
 161        "line_dash_array",
 162        "line_dash_phase",
 163        "line_join",
 164        "line_miter_limit",
 165        "line_width",
 166        "marker_alpha",
 167        "marker_color",
 168        "marker_radius",
 169        "marker_shape",
 170        "marker_size",
 171        "marker_type",
 172        "markers_only",
 173        "points",
 174        "smooth",
 175        "stroke",
 176        "subtype",
 177        "type",
 178        "visible",
 179        "xform_matrix",
 180    ]
 181
 182    def __init__(
 183        self,
 184        points: Sequence[PointType] | None = None,
 185        closed: bool = False,
 186        fill: bool | None = None,
 187        stroke: bool | None = None,
 188        line_width: float | None = None,
 189        line_color: Color | None = None,
 190        fill_color: Color | None = None,
 191        line_alpha: float | None = None,
 192        fill_alpha: float | None = None,
 193        line_cap: LineCap | None = None,
 194        line_dash_array: Sequence | None = None,
 195        line_dash_phase: float | None = None,
 196        line_join: LineJoin | None = None,
 197        line_miter_limit: float | None = None,
 198        draw_double: bool | None = None,
 199        draw_fillets: bool | None = None,
 200        draw_markers: bool | None = None,
 201        even_odd: bool | None = None,
 202        back_style: Any = None,
 203        double_distance: float | None = None,
 204        double_color: Color | None = None,
 205        fill_mode: FillMode | None = None,
 206        fillet_radius: float | None = None,
 207        gradient: Any = None,
 208        marker_alpha: float | None = None,
 209        marker_color: Color | None = None,
 210        marker_radius: float | None = None,
 211        marker_shape: Any = None,
 212        marker_size: float | None = None,
 213        marker_type: Any = None,
 214        markers_only: bool | None = None,
 215        smooth: bool | None = None,
 216        alpha: float | None = None,
 217        color: Color | None = None,
 218        subtype: Types = Types.SHAPE,
 219        xform_matrix: NDArray | None = None,
 220    ) -> None:
 221        """Initialize a Shape.
 222
 223        Args:
 224            points: Vertices as ``(x, y)`` pairs. Defaults to empty.
 225            closed: If True, treat as a closed polygon.
 226            fill: Whether to fill the interior.
 227            stroke: Whether to stroke the outline.
 228            alpha: Overall opacity override.
 229            color: Convenience color (may set fill/line depending on style).
 230            draw_double / draw_fillets / draw_markers: Stroke embellishments.
 231            back_style: Background style enum/value.
 232            double_distance / double_color: Double-line stroke options.
 233            fill_alpha / fill_color / fill_mode: Fill style.
 234            fillet_radius: Corner fillet radius when drawing fillets.
 235            gradient: Optional fill gradient.
 236            line_alpha / line_cap / line_color / line_dash_array /
 237                line_dash_phase / line_join / line_miter_limit / line_width:
 238                Stroke style.
 239            marker_*: Marker drawing options.
 240            even_odd: If True, use even-odd fill rule. Omitted uses
 241                ``user_defaults["even_odd"]`` at init.
 242            markers_only: If True, draw markers without the path.
 243            smooth: Prefer smooth curve rendering when applicable.
 244            subtype: Shape subtype. Defaults to ``Types.SHAPE``.
 245            xform_matrix: Optional initial transform.
 246
 247        Raises:
 248            ValueError: If ``subtype`` is not a ``Types`` member.
 249
 250        Examples:
 251            >>> s = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
 252            >>> s.vertices
 253            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0))
 254            >>> s.closed
 255            True
 256        """
 257
 258        self.id = get_unique_id(self)
 259        self._external = False
 260
 261        if points is None:
 262            self.primary_points = Points()
 263            self.closed = False
 264        else:
 265            self.closed, points = self._get_closed(points, closed)
 266            self.primary_points = Points(points)
 267            self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = True
 268        self.xform_matrix = get_transform(xform_matrix)
 269        self.type = Types.SHAPE
 270        self._init_from_style_kwargs(
 271            {
 272                "color": color,
 273                "alpha": alpha,
 274                "line_color": line_color,
 275                "fill_color": fill_color,
 276                "line_alpha": line_alpha,
 277                "fill_alpha": fill_alpha,
 278                "line_width": line_width,
 279                "fill": fill,
 280                "stroke": stroke,
 281                "line_dash_array": line_dash_array,
 282                "line_dash_phase": line_dash_phase,
 283                "line_cap": line_cap,
 284                "line_join": line_join,
 285                "line_miter_limit": line_miter_limit,
 286                "smooth": smooth,
 287                "back_style": back_style,
 288                "draw_double": draw_double,
 289                "draw_fillets": draw_fillets,
 290                "double_distance": double_distance,
 291                "double_color": double_color,
 292                "fill_mode": fill_mode,
 293                "fillet_radius": fillet_radius,
 294                "gradient": gradient,
 295                "draw_markers": draw_markers,
 296                "even_odd": even_odd,
 297                "marker_type": marker_type,
 298                "marker_size": marker_size,
 299                "marker_radius": marker_radius,
 300                "marker_alpha": marker_alpha,
 301                "marker_color": marker_color,
 302                "marker_shape": marker_shape,
 303                "markers_only": markers_only,
 304            }
 305        )
 306        if not check_subtype(subtype):
 307            raise ValueError(f"Invalid value for subtype: {subtype}")
 308        self.subtype = subtype
 309        self.visible = True
 310
 311        self._b_box = None
 312
 313    def _clear_geometry_caches(self) -> None:
 314        """Clear cached transformed geometry derived from vertices."""
 315        for attr in (
 316            "_final_coords",
 317            "_vertices",
 318            "_edge_lengths",
 319            "_total_length",
 320        ):
 321            if attr in self.__dict__:
 322                delattr(self, attr)
 323
 324    def _get_closed(
 325        self, points: Sequence[PointType], closed: bool
 326    ) -> tuple[bool, list[PointType]]:
 327        """Determine whether the shape should be considered closed.
 328
 329        Args:
 330            points: Vertices defining the shape.
 331            closed: User-specified closed flag.
 332
 333        Returns:
 334            ``(is_closed, vertices)`` with duplicate closing vertex removed
 335            when detected as a polygon.
 336        """
 337
 338        n = len(points)
 339        if n < 3:
 340            res = False
 341        else:
 342            points = [tuple(x[:2]) for x in points]
 343            polygon = self._is_polygon(points)
 344            res = bool(closed) or polygon
 345            if polygon:
 346                points.pop()
 347        return res, points
 348
 349    def __len__(self) -> int:
 350        """Return the number of points in the shape.
 351
 352        Returns:
 353            int: The number of primary points.
 354        """
 355        return len(self.primary_points)
 356
 357    def __str__(self) -> str:
 358        """Return a string representation of the shape.
 359
 360        Returns:
 361            str: A string representation of the shape.
 362        """
 363        if len(self.primary_points) == 0:
 364            res = "Shape()"
 365        elif len(self.primary_points) < 4:
 366            res = f"Shape({self.vertices})"
 367        else:
 368            res = f"Shape([{self.vertices[0]}, ..., {self.vertices[-1]}])"
 369        return res
 370
 371    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 372        """Return a string representation of the shape.
 373
 374        Returns:
 375            str: A string representation of the shape.
 376        """
 377        return self.__str__()
 378
 379    def __getitem__(
 380        self, subscript: int | float | slice
 381    ) -> PointType | list[PointType]:
 382        """Retrieve point(s) from the shape by index or slice.
 383
 384        Args:
 385            subscript: Integer index, fractional index (lerp along an edge),
 386                or slice over transformed vertices.
 387
 388        Returns:
 389            Transformed vertex or list of vertices.
 390
 391        Raises:
 392            TypeError: If the subscript type is invalid.
 393        """
 394        # Use cached final_coords instead of recalculating matrix multiplication
 395        final_coords = self.final_coords
 396
 397        if isinstance(subscript, slice):
 398            res = [tuple(coord[:2]) for coord in final_coords[subscript]]
 399        elif isinstance(subscript, float):
 400            if subscript.is_integer():
 401                subscript = int(subscript)
 402                coord = final_coords[subscript]
 403                res = (coord[0], coord[1])
 404            else:
 405                n = len(final_coords)
 406                index = floor(subscript)
 407                if self.closed:
 408                    next_index = (index + 1) % n
 409                else:
 410                    if subscript >= n - 1:
 411                        raise ValueError("Invalid index!")
 412                    else:
 413                        next_index = index + 1
 414                vertex = final_coords[index]
 415                next_vertex = final_coords[next_index]
 416                t = subscript - index
 417                res = lerp_point(vertex, next_vertex, t)
 418        else:
 419            coord = final_coords[subscript]
 420            res = (coord[0], coord[1])
 421        return res
 422
 423    def __setitem__(
 424        self,
 425        subscript: int | slice,
 426        value: PointType | Sequence[PointType] | Any,
 427    ) -> None:
 428        """Set the point(s) at the given subscript.
 429
 430        Args:
 431            subscript: Index or slice into ``primary_points``.
 432            value: Point(s) in canvas space (inverse-transformed before storage).
 433
 434        Raises:
 435            TypeError: If the subscript type is invalid.
 436        """
 437        if isinstance(subscript, slice):
 438            if is_nested_sequence(value):
 439                value = homogenize(value) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 440            else:
 441                value = homogenize([value]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 442            self.primary_points[
 443                subscript.start : subscript.stop : subscript.step
 444            ] = [tuple(x[:2]) for x in value]
 445            self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = True
 446        elif isinstance(subscript, int):
 447            value = homogenize([value]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 448            self.primary_points[subscript] = tuple(value[0][:2])
 449            self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = True
 450        else:
 451            raise TypeError("Invalid subscript type")
 452        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 453
 454    def __delitem__(self, subscript: int | slice) -> Self:
 455        """Delete the point(s) at the given subscript.
 456
 457        Args:
 458            subscript: Index or slice into ``primary_points``.
 459        """
 460        del self.primary_points[subscript]
 461        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 462
 463    def index(self, point: PointType, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> int:
 464        """Return the index of the given point.
 465
 466        Args:
 467            point: Vertex to locate in transformed coordinates.
 468            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['abs_tol']``.
 469
 470        Returns:
 471            int: The index of the point.
 472
 473        Examples:
 474            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 475            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 476            >>> int(rect.index((0, 0)))
 477            0
 478        """
 479        point = tuple(point[:2])
 480
 481        if abs_tol is None:
 482            abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
 483        ind = np.where(
 484            (np.isclose(self.vertices, point, atol=abs_tol)).all(axis=1)
 485        )[0][0]
 486
 487        return ind
 488
 489    def remove(self, point: PointType) -> Self:
 490        """Remove a point from the shape.
 491
 492        Args:
 493            point (PointType): The point to remove.
 494
 495        Examples:
 496            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 497            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0)])
 498            >>> line.remove((0, 0))
 499            Shape(((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 500            >>> line.vertices
 501            ((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0))
 502        """
 503        ind = self.vertices.index(point)
 504        self.primary_points.pop(ind)
 505        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 506
 507        return self
 508
 509    def append(self, point: PointType) -> Self:
 510        """Append a point to the shape.
 511
 512        Args:
 513            point (PointType): The point to append.
 514
 515        Examples:
 516            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 517            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0)])
 518            >>> line.append((40, 0))
 519            >>> line.vertices
 520            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 521        """
 522        point = homogenize([point]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 523        self.primary_points.append(tuple(point[0][:2]))
 524        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 525        return self
 526
 527    def insert(self, index: int, point: PointType) -> Self:
 528        """Insert a point at a given index.
 529
 530        Args:
 531            index (int): The index to insert the point at.
 532            point (PointType): The point to insert.
 533
 534        Examples:
 535            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 536            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0)])
 537            >>> line.insert(1, (40, 0))
 538            Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 539        """
 540        point = homogenize([point]) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 541        self.primary_points.insert(index, tuple(point[0][:2]))
 542        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 543
 544        return self
 545
 546    def extend(self, points: Sequence[PointType]) -> Self:
 547        """Extend the shape with a list of points.
 548
 549        Args:
 550            values (list[PointType]): The points to extend the shape with.
 551
 552        Examples:
 553            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 554            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0)])
 555            >>> line.extend([(40, 0), (80, 0)])
 556            Shape(((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
 557        """
 558        homogenized = homogenize(points) @ inv(self.xform_matrix)
 559        self.primary_points.extend([tuple(x[:2]) for x in homogenized])
 560        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 561
 562        return self
 563
 564    def pop(self, index: int = -1) -> PointType:
 565        """Pop a point from the shape.
 566
 567        Args:
 568            index (int, optional): The index to pop the point from, defaults to -1.
 569
 570        Returns:
 571            PointType: The popped point.
 572
 573        Examples:
 574            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 575            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
 576            >>> line.pop()
 577            (40.0, 0.0)
 578            >>> line.vertices
 579            ((0.0, 0.0),)
 580        """
 581        point = self.vertices[index]
 582        self.primary_points.pop(index)
 583        self._clear_geometry_caches()
 584
 585        return point
 586
 587    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[PointType]:
 588        """Return an iterator over the vertices of the shape.
 589
 590        Returns:
 591            Iterator over transformed ``vertices``.
 592        """
 593        return iter(self.vertices)
 594
 595    def _update(
 596        self,
 597        xform_matrix: array,
 598        reps: int = 0,
 599        take: slice | None = None,
 600        incr: float
 601        | tuple[float, float]
 602        | tuple[callable, Any]
 603        | tuple[InPlace, Any]
 604        | NDArray
 605        | Sequence[Sequence[float]]
 606        | None = None,
 607        dyn_ref: Callable | None = None,
 608        merge: bool = False,
 609        xform_type: TransformationType = None,
 610    ) -> Shape | Group:
 611        """Used internally. Update the shape with a transformation matrix.
 612
 613        Args:
 614            xform_matrix (array): The transformation matrix.
 615            reps (int, optional): The number of repetitions, defaults to 0.
 616            dyn_ref: Matrix factory built by the transform method when
 617                dynamic references are in use. Defaults to None.
 618
 619        Returns:
 620            Shape or Group: The updated shape or a group of shapes.
 621        """
 622        if reps == 0:
 623            fillet_radius = getattr(self, "fillet_radius", None)
 624            if fillet_radius:
 625                scale = max(decompose_transformations(xform_matrix)[2])
 626                self.fillet_radius = fillet_radius * scale
 627
 628            self.xform_matrix = self.xform_matrix @ xform_matrix
 629            self._clear_geometry_caches()
 630            res = self
 631        else:
 632            shapes = [self]
 633            shape = self
 634            if dyn_ref:
 635                pattern = Group()
 636                # Aliases shapes, so the pattern grows with the loop.
 637                pattern.elements = shapes
 638                targets = _Targets(self, pattern)
 639            else:
 640                targets = None
 641            for i in range(reps):
 642                shape = shape.copy()
 643                if targets is not None:
 644                    targets.active = shape
 645                xform_matrix = _next_xform_matrix(
 646                    xform_matrix, xform_type, incr, dyn_ref, targets, i
 647                )
 648                shape._update(xform_matrix)
 649                shapes.append(shape)
 650            res = Group(shapes)
 651
 652        if merge and reps > 0:
 653            merged = combine_shapes(res)
 654            for shape in merged:
 655                shape.copy_style(self)
 656            if len(merged) == 1:
 657                return merged[0]
 658            return merged
 659
 660        return res
 661
 662    def _translate_along_group(
 663        self, copies: Sequence[Shape], merge: bool
 664    ) -> Shape | Group:
 665        """Return a Group of this shape plus extra ``translate_along`` copies."""
 666        result = Group([self, *copies])
 667        if merge:
 668            return result.merge_shapes()
 669        return result
 670
 671    def __hash__(self) -> int:
 672        return hash(self.id)
 673
 674    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
 675        """Check if the shape is equal to another shape.
 676
 677        Args:
 678            other: Object to compare (must be a ``Shape`` with matching data).
 679
 680        Returns:
 681            bool: True if the shapes are equal, False otherwise.
 682        """
 683        if not hasattr(other, "type"):
 684            return False
 685        if other.type != Types.SHAPE:
 686            return False
 687
 688        len1 = len(self)
 689        len2 = len(other)
 690        if len1 == 0 and len2 == 0:
 691            res = True
 692        elif len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
 693            res = False
 694        elif isinstance(other, Shape) and len1 == len2:
 695            res = allclose(
 696                self.xform_matrix,
 697                other.xform_matrix,
 698                rtol=runtime_defaults["rel_tol"],
 699                atol=runtime_defaults["abs_tol"],
 700            ) and allclose(
 701                self.primary_points.nd_array,
 702                other.primary_points.nd_array,
 703                rtol=runtime_defaults["rel_tol"],
 704                atol=runtime_defaults["abs_tol"],
 705            )
 706        else:
 707            res = False
 708
 709        return res
 710
 711    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
 712        """Return whether the shape has any points.
 713
 714        Returns:
 715            bool: True if the shape has points, False otherwise.
 716        """
 717        return len(self.primary_points) > 0
 718
 719    def is_clockwise(self) -> bool:
 720        """Check if the shape is oriented clockwise.
 721
 722        Returns:
 723            bool: True if the shape is oriented clockwise, False otherwise.
 724
 725        Examples:
 726            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 727            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 728            >>> bool(rect.is_clockwise())
 729            False
 730        """
 731        if not self.closed:
 732            raise ValueError("Shape must be closed to check orientation")
 733        vertices = self.vertices
 734        area = polygon_area(vertices)
 735        return area < 0
 736
 737    def reordered(self, index: int) -> Self:
 738        """Return a copy of the shape starting from a point
 739        at the given index.
 740
 741        Args:
 742            index: Vertex index that becomes the new start (closed shapes only).
 743
 744        Returns:
 745            Shape: The shape with the starting point set.
 746
 747        Examples:
 748            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 749            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 750            >>> reordered = rect.reordered(1)
 751            >>> reordered.vertices
 752            ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0))
 753        """
 754        if not isinstance(index, int):
 755            raise TypeError("Index must be an integer")
 756        if not self.closed:
 757            raise ValueError("Shape must be closed to start from a point")
 758
 759        if index == 0:
 760            res = self.copy()
 761        else:
 762            shape = self.copy()
 763            vertices = shape.vertices
 764            shape[:] = vertices[index:] + vertices[:index]
 765            res = shape
 766
 767        return res
 768
 769    def lerp(self, edge: int, t: float) -> PointType:
 770        """Given an edge index and t value (between 0 and 1)
 771        returns the corresponding interpolated point.
 772
 773        Examples:
 774            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 775            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 776            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.lerp(0, 0.5)[:2])
 777            (20.0, 0.0)
 778        """
 779        return lerp_point(*self.edges[edge], t)
 780
 781    def merge_collinears(self) -> Shape:
 782        """Merge collinear edges into a single polyline.
 783
 784        Examples:
 785            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 786            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (40, 0)])
 787            >>> merged = line.merge_collinears()
 788            >>> merged.vertices
 789            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 790        """
 791        return Group([self]).merge_shapes()[0]
 792
 793    def merge(
 794        self,
 795        other: Shape,
 796        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 797        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 798    ) -> Shape:
 799        """Return a new polyline by joining ``other`` after this shape.
 800
 801        Both shapes must be open. ``self[-1]`` must meet ``other[0]``
 802        within ``abs_tol``. The duplicated join vertex is dropped. If
 803        the joining edges are collinear, the join vertex is removed as
 804        well. Inputs are not mutated. Use ``connect`` to append in place.
 805
 806        Args:
 807            other: Open polyline whose first vertex meets this shape's last.
 808            rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 809            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 810
 811        Returns:
 812            Shape: A new open polyline.
 813
 814        Raises:
 815            ValueError: If either shape is closed, either has fewer than
 816                two vertices, or the endpoints do not meet.
 817
 818        Examples:
 819            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 820            >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
 821            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
 822            >>> a.merge(b).vertices
 823            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 824            >>> c = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (20, 80)])
 825            >>> a.merge(c).vertices
 826            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))
 827        """
 828        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 829        if self.closed or other.closed:
 830            raise ValueError("Only open polylines can be merged")
 831        if len(self) < 2 or len(other) < 2:
 832            raise ValueError("Both shapes must have at least two vertices")
 833        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 834        if not close_points_square(self[-1], other[0], dist2=abs_tol2):
 835            raise ValueError("Shapes are not connected: self[-1] must equal other[0]")
 836        verts1 = self.as_list()
 837        verts2 = other.as_list()
 838        if collinear_segments(
 839            self.edges[-1], other.edges[0], rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
 840        ):
 841            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2[1:]
 842        else:
 843            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2
 844
 845        return Shape(vertices, closed=False)
 846
 847    def connect(self, other: Shape) -> Self:
 848        """Connect two shapes by adding the other shape's vertices to self.
 849
 850        Args:
 851            other: Shape whose vertices are appended.
 852
 853        Examples:
 854            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 855            >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
 856            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
 857            >>> a.connect(b)
 858            Shape([(0.0, 0.0), ..., (40.0, 0.0)])
 859            >>> a.vertices
 860            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
 861        """
 862        self.extend(other.vertices)
 863
 864        return self
 865
 866    def _chain_vertices(
 867        self,
 868        verts1: Sequence[PointType],
 869        verts2: Sequence[PointType],
 870        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 871        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 872    ) -> list[PointType] | None:
 873        """Chain two sets of vertices if they are connected.
 874
 875        Args:
 876            verts1 (list[PointType]): The first set of vertices.
 877            verts2 (list[PointType]): The second set of vertices.
 878            rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 879            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 880
 881        Returns:
 882            list[PointType] or None: The chained vertices or None if the vertices cannot be chained.
 883        """
 884        _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 885        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 886        start1, end1 = verts1[0], verts1[-1]
 887        start2, end2 = verts2[0], verts2[-1]
 888        same_starts = close_points_square(start1, start2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 889        same_ends = close_points_square(end1, end2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 890        if same_starts and same_ends:
 891            res = verts1
 892        elif close_points_square(end1, start2, dist2=abs_tol2):
 893            verts2.pop(0)
 894        elif close_points_square(start1, end2, dist2=abs_tol2):
 895            verts2.reverse()
 896            verts1.reverse()
 897            verts2.pop(0)
 898        elif same_starts:
 899            verts2.reverse()
 900            verts2.pop(-1)
 901            start = verts2[:]
 902            end = verts1[:]
 903            verts1 = start
 904            verts2 = end
 905        elif same_ends:
 906            verts2.reverse()
 907            verts2.pop(0)
 908        else:
 909            return None
 910        if same_starts and same_ends:
 911            all_verts = verts1 + verts2
 912            if not right_handed(all_verts):
 913                all_verts.reverse()
 914            res = all_verts
 915        else:
 916            res = verts1 + verts2
 917
 918        return res
 919
 920    def _is_polygon(self, vertices: Sequence[PointType]) -> bool:
 921        """Return True if the vertices form a polygon.
 922
 923        Args:
 924            vertices (list[PointType]): The vertices to check.
 925
 926        Returns:
 927            bool: True if the vertices form a polygon, False otherwise.
 928        """
 929        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
 930        return close_points_square(
 931            vertices[0][:2], vertices[-1][:2], dist2=abs_tol2
 932        )
 933
 934    def as_array(self, homogeneous: bool = False) -> NDArray:
 935        """Return the vertices as an array.
 936
 937        Args:
 938            homogeneous: If True, return homogeneous ``final_coords``.
 939
 940        Returns:
 941            ndarray: The vertices as an array.
 942
 943        Examples:
 944            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 945            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 946            >>> [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in rect.as_array()]
 947            [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
 948        """
 949        if homogeneous:
 950            # Use cached final_coords to avoid redundant matrix multiplication
 951            res = self.final_coords
 952        else:
 953            res = array(self.vertices)
 954        return res
 955
 956    def as_list(self) -> list[PointType]:
 957        """Return the vertices as a list of tuples.
 958
 959        Returns:
 960            list[tuple]: The vertices as a list of tuples.
 961
 962        Examples:
 963            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 964            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
 965            >>> line.as_list()
 966            [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 967        """
 968        return list(self.vertices)
 969
 970    @property
 971    def final_coords(self) -> NDArray:
 972        """The final coordinates of the shape. primary_points @ xform_matrix.
 973
 974        Returns:
 975            ndarray: The final coordinates of the shape.
 976
 977        Examples:
 978            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 979            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 980            >>> [(float(x), float(y), float(w)) for x, y, w in rect.final_coords]
 981            [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 40.0, 1.0), (0.0, 40.0, 1.0)]
 982        """
 983        if self.primary_points:
 984            # Cache the expensive matrix multiplication
 985            if (
 986                "_final_coords" not in self.__dict__
 987                or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
 988            ):
 989                self._final_coords = (
 990                    self.primary_points.homogen_coords @ self.xform_matrix
 991                )
 992            res = self._final_coords
 993        else:
 994            res = array([])
 995
 996        return res
 997
 998    @property
 999    def angle(self) -> float:
1000        """Orientation angle of the shape (radians).
1001
1002        Examples:
1003            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1004            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1005            >>> float(line.angle)
1006            0.0
1007        """
1008        res = decompose_transformations(self.xform_matrix)[1]
1009        return positive_angle(res)
1010
1011    @property
1012    def orientation(self) -> float:
1013        """Orientation angle of the shape (alias of ``angle``).
1014
1015        Examples:
1016            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1017            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1018            >>> float(line.orientation)
1019            0.0
1020        """
1021        return self.angle
1022
1023    @property
1024    def vertices(self) -> tuple[PointType]:
1025        """The final coordinates of the shape.
1026
1027        Returns:
1028            tuple: The final coordinates of the shape.
1029
1030        Examples:
1031            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1032            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1033            >>> rect.vertices
1034            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
1035        """
1036
1037        if self.primary_points:
1038            # Cache vertices computation and only recompute when data changes
1039            if (
1040                "_vertices" not in self.__dict__
1041                or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1042            ):
1043                res = tuple((x[0], x[1]) for x in (self.final_coords[:, :2]))
1044                self._vertices = res
1045                self.primary_points.nd_array_changed = False
1046            else:
1047                res = self._vertices
1048        else:
1049            res = ()
1050
1051        return res
1052
1053    @property
1054    def edge_lengths(self) -> list[float]:
1055        """Return the lengths of the shape edges.
1056
1057        For closed shapes, the closing edge from the last vertex back to the
1058        first is included.
1059
1060        Returns:
1061            list[float]: Edge lengths in vertex order.
1062
1063        Examples:
1064            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1065            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (30, 40), (60, 40)])
1066            >>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in line.edge_lengths]
1067            [50.0, 30.0]
1068            >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (3, 0), (3, 4)], closed=True)
1069            >>> [round(float(x), 6) for x in tri.edge_lengths]
1070            [3.0, 4.0, 5.0]
1071        """
1072        if not self.primary_points:
1073            return []
1074        if (
1075            "_edge_lengths" not in self.__dict__
1076            or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1077        ):
1078            self._edge_lengths = tuple(
1079                distance(*edge) for edge in self.edges
1080            )
1081        return list(self._edge_lengths)
1082
1083    @property
1084    def vertex_pairs(self) -> list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]:
1085        """Return a list of connected pairs of vertices.
1086
1087        Returns:
1088            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of connected pairs of vertices.
1089
1090        Examples:
1091            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1092            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1093            >>> rect.vertex_pairs
1094            [((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0))]
1095        """
1096        vertices = list(self.vertices)
1097        if self.closed:
1098            vertices.append(vertices[0])
1099        return connected_pairs(vertices)
1100
1101    @property
1102    def orig_coords(self) -> NDArray:
1103        """The primary points in homogeneous coordinates.
1104
1105        Returns:
1106            ndarray: The primary points in homogeneous coordinates.
1107
1108        Examples:
1109            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1110            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1111            >>> [(float(x), float(y), float(w)) for x, y, w in rect.orig_coords]
1112            [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 0.0, 1.0), (40.0, 40.0, 1.0), (0.0, 40.0, 1.0)]
1113        """
1114        return self.primary_points.homogen_coords
1115
1116    @property
1117    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
1118        """Return the bounding box of the shape.
1119
1120        Returns:
1121            BoundingBox: The bounding box of the shape.
1122
1123        Examples:
1124            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1125            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1126            >>> float(rect.b_box.width)
1127            40.0
1128        """
1129        if self.primary_points:
1130            self._b_box = bounding_box(self.final_coords)
1131        else:
1132            self._b_box = bounding_box([(0, 0)])
1133        return self._b_box
1134
1135    @property
1136    def area(self) -> float:
1137        """Return the area of the shape.
1138
1139        Returns:
1140            float: The area of the shape.
1141
1142        Examples:
1143            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1144            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1145            >>> float(rect.area)
1146            1600.0
1147        """
1148        if self.closed:
1149            vertices = self.vertices[:]
1150            abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1151            if not close_points_square(
1152                vertices[0], vertices[-1], dist2=abs_tol2
1153            ):
1154                vertices = list(vertices) + [vertices[0]]
1155            res = polygon_area(vertices)
1156        else:
1157            res = 0
1158
1159        return res
1160
1161    @property
1162    def total_length(self) -> float:
1163        """Return the total length of the shape.
1164
1165        Returns:
1166            float: The total length of the shape.
1167
1168        Examples:
1169            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1170            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
1171            >>> line.total_length
1172            80.0
1173            >>> line2 = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
1174            >>> round(float(line2.total_length), 6)
1175            136.568542
1176        """
1177        if not self.primary_points:
1178            return 0.0
1179        if (
1180            "_total_length" not in self.__dict__
1181            or self.primary_points.nd_array_changed
1182        ):
1183            self._total_length = float(sum(self.edge_lengths))
1184        return self._total_length
1185
1186    @property
1187    def is_polygon(self) -> bool:
1188        """Return True if 'closed'.
1189
1190        Returns:
1191            bool: True if the shape is closed, False otherwise.
1192
1193        Examples:
1194            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1195            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1196            >>> rect.is_polygon
1197            True
1198        """
1199        return self.closed

1201    def clear(self) -> Self:
1202        """Clear all points and reset the style attributes.
1203
1204        Returns:
1205            None
1206
1207        Examples:
1208            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1209            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1210            >>> rect.clear()
1211            Shape()
1212            >>> rect.vertices
1213            ()
1214        """
1215        self.primary_points = Points()
1216        self.xform_matrix = identity_matrix()
1217        self._b_box = None
1218        self._clear_geometry_caches()
1219
1220        return self
1221
1222    def count(self, point: PointType) -> int:
1223        """Return the number of times the point is found in the shape.
1224
1225        Args:
1226            point (PointType): The point to count.
1227
1228        Returns:
1229            int: The number of times the point is found in the shape.
1230
1231        Examples:
1232            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1233            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1234            >>> rect.count((0, 0))
1235            1
1236        """
1237        verts = self.orig_coords @ self.xform_matrix
1238        verts = verts[:, :2]
1239        n = verts.shape[0]
1240        point = array(point[:2])
1241        values = np.tile(point, (n, 1))
1242        col1 = (verts[:, 0] - values[:, 0]) ** 2
1243        col2 = (verts[:, 1] - values[:, 1]) ** 2
1244        distances = col1 + col2
1245        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1246
1247        return np.count_nonzero(distances <= abs_tol2)
1248
1249    def copy(self) -> Shape:
1250        """Return a copy of the shape.
1251
1252        Returns:
1253            Shape: A copy of the shape.
1254
1255        Examples:
1256            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1257            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1258            >>> copy = rect.copy()
1259            >>> copy == rect
1260            True
1261            >>> copy is rect
1262            False
1263        """
1264        self._b_box = None
1265        return deepcopy(self)

1267    def segment(
1268        self, i: int, j: int, midpoints: bool = False
1269    ) -> tuple[PointType]:
1270        """Returns a line segment with shape[i] and shape[j] endpoints.
1271        If midpoints is True then returns a line segment between midpoints
1272        of the shape.edges[i] and shape.edges[j]
1273
1274        Examples:
1275            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1276            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1277            >>> p0, p1 = rect.segment(0, 2)
1278            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p0[:2])
1279            (0.0, 0.0)
1280            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p1[:2])
1281            (40.0, 40.0)
1282        """
1283        if midpoints:
1284            res = (self.edge_midpoint(i), self.edge_midpoint(j))
1285        else:
1286            res = (self[i], self[j])
1287
1288        return res
1289
1290    def edge_midpoint(self, i: int) -> PointType:
1291        """Return the midpoint of shape.edges[i].
1292
1293        Examples:
1294            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1295            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1296            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.edge_midpoint(0)[:2])
1297            (20.0, 0.0)
1298        """
1299
1300        n = len(self)
1301        edge = (self[i], self[(i + 1) % n])
1302
1303        return midpoint(*edge)
1304
1305    @property
1306    def edge_midpoints(self) -> list[PointType]:
1307        """Return a list of the edge midpoints.
1308
1309        Examples:
1310            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1311            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1312            >>> rect.edge_midpoints
1313            [(20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0), (20.0, 40.0), (0.0, 20.0)]
1314        """
1315        edges = self.edges
1316
1317        return [midpoint(*edge) for edge in edges]
1318
1319    @property
1320    def edges(self) -> list[LineType]:
1321        """Return a list of the edges of the shape.
1322
1323        Edges are represented as tuples of points:
1324        edge: ((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
1325        edges: [((x1, y1), (x2, y2)), ((x2, y2), (x3, y3)), ...]
1326
1327        Returns:
1328            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of edges.
1329
1330        Examples:
1331            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1332            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1333            >>> rect.edges
1334            (((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1335        """
1336        vertices = list(self.vertices[:])
1337        if self.closed:
1338            vertices.append(vertices[0])
1339
1340        return tuple(connected_pairs(vertices))
1341
1342    @property
1343    def midpoints(self) -> list[PointType]:
1344        """Returns a list of the midpoints of the edges.
1345
1346        Examples:
1347            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1348            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1349            >>> rect.midpoints
1350            [(20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0), (20.0, 40.0), (0.0, 20.0)]
1351        """
1352        return [midpoint(*edge) for edge in self.edges]
1353
1354    @property
1355    def segments(self) -> list[LineType]:
1356        """Return a list of edges.
1357
1358        Edges are represented as tuples of points:
1359        edge: ((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
1360        edges: [((x1, y1), (x2, y2)), ((x2, y2), (x3, y3)), ...]
1361
1362        Returns:
1363            list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]: A list of edges.
1364
1365        Examples:
1366            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1367            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1368            >>> rect.segments
1369            (((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)), ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)), ((0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1370        """
1371
1372        return self.edges

1374    def reverse(self) -> Self:
1375        """Reverse the order of the vertices.
1376
1377        Returns:
1378            None
1379
1380        Examples:
1381            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1382            >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
1383            >>> tri.reverse()
1384            Shape(((40.0, 40.0), (40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0)))
1385            >>> tri.vertices
1386            ((40.0, 40.0), (40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0))
1387        """
1388        self.primary_points.reverse()
1389        self._clear_geometry_caches()
1390
1391        return self

1467    @property
1468    def midpoint(self) -> PointType:
1469        """Center of the axis-aligned bounding box.

1471        Examples:

1475            (20.0, 20.0)
1476        """
1477        x1, y1 = self.southwest
1478        x2, y2 = self.northeast

1480        xc = (x1 + x2) / 2
1481        yc = (y1 + y2) / 2

1713    def get_inflated_b_box(
1714        self,
1715        left_margin: float | None = None,
1716        bottom_margin: float | None = None,
1717        right_margin: float | None = None,
1718        top_margin: float | None = None,
1719    ) -> BoundingBox:
1720        """Return a bounding box expanded by the given margins.
1721
1722        Args:
1723            left_margin: Outward offset on the left; other margins default from it.
1724            bottom_margin: Outward offset on the bottom.
1725            right_margin: Outward offset on the right.
1726            top_margin: Outward offset on the top.
1727
1728        Returns:
1729            Inflated ``BoundingBox``.
1730
1731        Examples:
1732            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1733            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1734            >>> inflated = rect.get_inflated_b_box(1)
1735            >>> inflated.corners
1736            ((-1.0, 41.0), (-1.0, -1.0), (41.0, -1.0), (41.0, 41.0))
1737        """
1738
1739        if bottom_margin is None:
1740            bottom_margin = left_margin
1741        if right_margin is None:
1742            right_margin = left_margin
1743        if top_margin is None:
1744            top_margin = bottom_margin
1745
1746        x, y = self.southwest[:2]
1747        southwest = (x - left_margin, y - bottom_margin)
1748
1749        x, y = self.northeast[:2]
1750        northeast = (x + right_margin, y + top_margin)
1751
1752        return BoundingBox(southwest, northeast)
1753
1754    def offset_line(
1755        self, side: Side | str, offset: float
1756    ) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
1757        """Offset a bounding-box edge outward (negative ``offset`` goes inward).
1758
1759        Args:
1760            side: ``Side`` enum member or name accepted by ``BoundingBox``.
1761            offset: Perpendicular offset distance.
1762
1763        Returns:
1764            Offset segment as two points.
1765
1766        Examples:
1767            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1768            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1769            >>> rect.offset_line('left', 1)
1770            ((-1.0, 0.0), (-1.0, 40.0))
1771        """
1772        return self.b_box.offset_line(side, offset)
1773

1776    ) -> PointType:
1777        """Return a point offset from a bounding-box anchor.

1779        Args:
1780            anchor: ``Anchor`` enum member or alias.
1781            dx: Horizontal offset.
1782            dy: Vertical offset.
1783
1784        Returns:
1785            Offset point in canvas coordinates.
1786

2078    def reorder_vertices(
2079        self, value: PointType, index: int = 0, tol: float | None = None
2080    ) -> Shape | None:
2081        """If index is not given, the vertex with the given value will be
2082        the first index.
2083        If index is given, the vertex with the given value will be
2084        at the given index.
2085        The rest of the indices will be shifted accordingly.
2086
2087        Shape must be closed.
2088
2089        Args:
2090            index (int): The target index.
2091            value (PointType): The vertex to relocate at the given index.
2092
2093        Returns:
2094            Shape: A new shape with the adjusted vertices.
2095
2096        Examples:
2097            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2098            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2099            >>> reordered = rect.reorder_vertices((40, 40))
2100            >>> reordered.vertices
2101            ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
2102        """
2103
2104        if not isinstance(value, Sequence) or len(value) < 2:
2105            raise TypeError("Value must be a [x, y] sequence")
2106
2107        if self.closed:
2108            vertices = list(self.vertices)
2109            if value in vertices:
2110                cur_index = vertices.index(value)
2111            else:
2112                if tol is None:
2113                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2114                dist, ind = min(
2115                    [(distance(value, v), i) for i, v in enumerate(vertices)],
2116                    key=lambda x: x[0],
2117                )
2118                if dist < tol:
2119                    cur_index = ind
2120                else:
2121                    return None
2122
2123            shift = index - cur_index
2124            if shift == 0:
2125                return None
2126
2127            if value in vertices:
2128                new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2129            else:
2130                if tol is None:
2131                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2132                if distance(value, vertices[cur_index]) < tol:
2133                    new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2134                else:
2135                    new_vertices = None
2136            if new_vertices is not None:
2137                res = self.copy()
2138                res[:] = new_vertices
2139            else:
2140                res = None
2141        else:
2142            res = None
2143
2144        return res

Polyline/polygon drawable with style and affine transform state.

Constructed from a sequence of points. When closed is True (or the first and last points coincide), the shape is treated as a polygon for fill and boolean operations. If the first and last points coincide then the last point is removed.

Omitted style arguments are stored from user_defaults at init. color and alpha stay unset unless passed. color sets both line_color and fill_color. alpha sets both line_alpha and fill_alpha. Reading a line_color / fill_color / line_alpha / fill_alpha that was later set to None returns the matching configured default. Use sg.doc(sg.Shape) to see the defaults.

Style color/alpha properties and copy_style come from CommonStyle.

Attributes:
  • primary_points: Points storage.
  • xform_matrix: 3×3 affine transform (row form).
  • closed: Whether the outline is closed.
  • fill / stroke: Draw fill and/or stroke.
  • line_width / line_color / fill_color: Common style attributes.
  • subtype: Shape subtype (Types.SHAPE, Types.CIRCLE, …).
  • id: Unique object id.
Examples:
>>> s = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
>>> s.vertices
((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0))
>>> s.width
40.0

def index(self, point: Sequence[float], abs_tol: float | None = None) -> int: 
463    def index(self, point: PointType, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> int:
464        """Return the index of the given point.
465
466        Args:
467            point: Vertex to locate in transformed coordinates.
468            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['abs_tol']``.
469
470        Returns:
471            int: The index of the point.
472
473        Examples:
474            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
475            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
476            >>> int(rect.index((0, 0)))
477            0
478        """
479        point = tuple(point[:2])
480
481        if abs_tol is None:
482            abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
483        ind = np.where(
484            (np.isclose(self.vertices, point, atol=abs_tol)).all(axis=1)
485        )[0][0]
486
487        return ind

def remove(self, point: Sequence[float]) -> Self: 
489    def remove(self, point: PointType) -> Self:
490        """Remove a point from the shape.
491
492        Args:
493            point (PointType): The point to remove.
494
495        Examples:
496            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
497            >>> line = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0)])
498            >>> line.remove((0, 0))
499            Shape(((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0)))
500            >>> line.vertices
501            ((40.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0))
502        """
503        ind = self.vertices.index(point)
504        self.primary_points.pop(ind)
505        self._clear_geometry_caches()

737    def reordered(self, index: int) -> Self:
738        """Return a copy of the shape starting from a point
739        at the given index.
740
741        Args:
742            index: Vertex index that becomes the new start (closed shapes only).
743

745            Shape: The shape with the starting point set.
746

749            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)

751            >>> reordered.vertices
752            ((40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0))
753        """
754        if not isinstance(index, int):
755            raise TypeError("Index must be an integer")
756        if not self.closed:
757            raise ValueError("Shape must be closed to start from a point")
758
759        if index == 0:
760            res = self.copy()
761        else:
762            shape = self.copy()
763            vertices = shape.vertices
764            shape[:] = vertices[index:] + vertices[:index]
765            res = shape
766
767        return res

def merge( self, other: Shape, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> Shape: 
793    def merge(
794        self,
795        other: Shape,
796        rel_tol: float | None = None,
797        abs_tol: float | None = None,
798    ) -> Shape:
799        """Return a new polyline by joining ``other`` after this shape.
800
801        Both shapes must be open. ``self[-1]`` must meet ``other[0]``
802        within ``abs_tol``. The duplicated join vertex is dropped. If
803        the joining edges are collinear, the join vertex is removed as
804        well. Inputs are not mutated. Use ``connect`` to append in place.
805
806        Args:
807            other: Open polyline whose first vertex meets this shape's last.
808            rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
809            abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
810
811        Returns:
812            Shape: A new open polyline.
813
814        Raises:
815            ValueError: If either shape is closed, either has fewer than
816                two vertices, or the endpoints do not meet.
817
818        Examples:
819            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
820            >>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
821            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
822            >>> a.merge(b).vertices
823            ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
824            >>> c = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (20, 80)])
825            >>> a.merge(c).vertices
826            ((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))
827        """
828        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
829        if self.closed or other.closed:
830            raise ValueError("Only open polylines can be merged")
831        if len(self) < 2 or len(other) < 2:
832            raise ValueError("Both shapes must have at least two vertices")
833        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
834        if not close_points_square(self[-1], other[0], dist2=abs_tol2):
835            raise ValueError("Shapes are not connected: self[-1] must equal other[0]")
836        verts1 = self.as_list()
837        verts2 = other.as_list()
838        if collinear_segments(
839            self.edges[-1], other.edges[0], rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
840        ):
841            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2[1:]
842        else:
843            vertices = verts1[:-1] + verts2
844
845        return Shape(vertices, closed=False)

Return a new polyline by joining other after this shape.

Both shapes must be open. self[-1] must meet other[0] within abs_tol. The duplicated join vertex is dropped. If the joining edges are collinear, the join vertex is removed as well. Inputs are not mutated. Use connect to append in place.

Arguments:
  • other: Open polyline whose first vertex meets this shape's last.
  • rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to runtime_defaults["rel_tol"].
  • abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to runtime_defaults["abs_tol"].
Returns:

Shape: A new open polyline.

Raises:
  • ValueError: If either shape is closed, either has fewer than two vertices, or the endpoints do not meet.
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> a = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0)])
>>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])
>>> a.merge(b).vertices
((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
>>> c = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (20, 80)])
>>> a.merge(c).vertices
((0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))

848        """Connect two shapes by adding the other shape's vertices to self.

856            >>> b = sg.Shape([(20, 0), (40, 0)])

def count(self, point: Sequence[float]) -> int: 
1222    def count(self, point: PointType) -> int:
1223        """Return the number of times the point is found in the shape.
1224
1225        Args:
1226            point (PointType): The point to count.
1227
1228        Returns:
1229            int: The number of times the point is found in the shape.
1230
1231        Examples:
1232            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1233            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1234            >>> rect.count((0, 0))
1235            1
1236        """
1237        verts = self.orig_coords @ self.xform_matrix
1238        verts = verts[:, :2]
1239        n = verts.shape[0]
1240        point = array(point[:2])
1241        values = np.tile(point, (n, 1))
1242        col1 = (verts[:, 0] - values[:, 0]) ** 2
1243        col2 = (verts[:, 1] - values[:, 1]) ** 2
1244        distances = col1 + col2
1245        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1246
1247        return np.count_nonzero(distances <= abs_tol2)

  • point (PointType): The point to count.

int: The number of times the point is found in the shape.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
>>> rect.count((0, 0))
1

def segment(self, i: int, j: int, midpoints: bool = False) -> tuple[Sequence[float]]: 
1267    def segment(
1268        self, i: int, j: int, midpoints: bool = False
1269    ) -> tuple[PointType]:
1270        """Returns a line segment with shape[i] and shape[j] endpoints.
1271        If midpoints is True then returns a line segment between midpoints
1272        of the shape.edges[i] and shape.edges[j]
1273
1274        Examples:
1275            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1276            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1277            >>> p0, p1 = rect.segment(0, 2)
1278            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p0[:2])
1279            (0.0, 0.0)
1280            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in p1[:2])
1281            (40.0, 40.0)
1282        """
1283        if midpoints:
1284            res = (self.edge_midpoint(i), self.edge_midpoint(j))
1285        else:
1286            res = (self[i], self[j])
1287
1288        return res

Returns a line segment with shape[i] and shape[j] endpoints. If midpoints is True then returns a line segment between midpoints of the shape.edges[i] and shape.edges[j]

def edge_midpoint(self, i: int) -> Sequence[float]: 
1290    def edge_midpoint(self, i: int) -> PointType:
1291        """Return the midpoint of shape.edges[i].
1292
1293        Examples:
1294            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1295            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1296            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in rect.edge_midpoint(0)[:2])
1297            (20.0, 0.0)
1298        """
1299
1300        n = len(self)
1301        edge = (self[i], self[(i + 1) % n])
1302
1303        return midpoint(*edge)

def get_inflated_b_box( self, left_margin: float | None = None, bottom_margin: float | None = None, right_margin: float | None = None, top_margin: float | None = None) -> simetri.geom.bbox.BoundingBox: 
1713    def get_inflated_b_box(
1714        self,
1715        left_margin: float | None = None,
1716        bottom_margin: float | None = None,
1717        right_margin: float | None = None,
1718        top_margin: float | None = None,
1719    ) -> BoundingBox:
1720        """Return a bounding box expanded by the given margins.
1721
1722        Args:
1723            left_margin: Outward offset on the left; other margins default from it.
1724            bottom_margin: Outward offset on the bottom.
1725            right_margin: Outward offset on the right.
1726            top_margin: Outward offset on the top.
1727
1728        Returns:
1729            Inflated ``BoundingBox``.
1730
1731        Examples:
1732            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1733            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1734            >>> inflated = rect.get_inflated_b_box(1)
1735            >>> inflated.corners
1736            ((-1.0, 41.0), (-1.0, -1.0), (41.0, -1.0), (41.0, 41.0))
1737        """
1738
1739        if bottom_margin is None:
1740            bottom_margin = left_margin
1741        if right_margin is None:
1742            right_margin = left_margin
1743        if top_margin is None:
1744            top_margin = bottom_margin
1745
1746        x, y = self.southwest[:2]
1747        southwest = (x - left_margin, y - bottom_margin)
1748
1749        x, y = self.northeast[:2]
1750        northeast = (x + right_margin, y + top_margin)
1751
1752        return BoundingBox(southwest, northeast)

Return a bounding box expanded by the given margins.

Arguments:
  • left_margin: Outward offset on the left; other margins default from it.
  • bottom_margin: Outward offset on the bottom.
  • right_margin: Outward offset on the right.
  • top_margin: Outward offset on the top.
Returns:

Inflated BoundingBox.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
>>> inflated = rect.get_inflated_b_box(1)
>>> inflated.corners
((-1.0, 41.0), (-1.0, -1.0), (41.0, -1.0), (41.0, 41.0))

def centered( self, item: Shape | simetri.group.batch.Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0) -> Sequence[float]: 
1795    def centered(
1796        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1797    ) -> PointType:
1798        """
1799        Get the center of the reference item.
1800
1801        Args:
1802            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1803            dx (float): The x offset.
1804            dy (float): The y offset.
1805
1806        Returns:
1807            PointType: The item.midpoint of the reference item's bounding-box.
1808
1809        Examples:
1810            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1811            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1812            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1813            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.centered(ref)[:2])
1814            (20.0, 20.0)
1815        """
1816
1817        x, y = item.midpoint[:2]
1818        x += dx
1819        y += dy
1820        return x, y

1822    def left_of(
1823        self, item: Shape | Group, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0
1824    ) -> PointType:
1825        """
1826        Get the item.west of the reference item.
1827
1828        Args:
1829            item (object): The reference item. Shape or Group.
1830            dx (float): The x offset.
1831            dy (float): The y offset.
1832
1833        Returns:
1834            PointType: The item.west of the reference item's bounding-box.
1835
1836        Examples:
1837            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1838            >>> ref = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1839            >>> small = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1840            >>> tuple(float(x) for x in small.left_of(ref)[:2])
1841            (-40.0, 20.0)
1842        """
1843        x, y = item.west[:2]
1844        w2 = self.width / 2
1845        x += dx - w2
1846        y += dy
1847        return x, y

def reorder_vertices( self, value: Sequence[float], index: int = 0, tol: float | None = None) -> Shape | None: 
2078    def reorder_vertices(
2079        self, value: PointType, index: int = 0, tol: float | None = None
2080    ) -> Shape | None:
2081        """If index is not given, the vertex with the given value will be
2082        the first index.
2083        If index is given, the vertex with the given value will be
2084        at the given index.
2085        The rest of the indices will be shifted accordingly.
2086
2087        Shape must be closed.
2088
2089        Args:
2090            index (int): The target index.
2091            value (PointType): The vertex to relocate at the given index.
2092
2093        Returns:
2094            Shape: A new shape with the adjusted vertices.
2095
2096        Examples:
2097            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2098            >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2099            >>> reordered = rect.reorder_vertices((40, 40))
2100            >>> reordered.vertices
2101            ((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))
2102        """
2103
2104        if not isinstance(value, Sequence) or len(value) < 2:
2105            raise TypeError("Value must be a [x, y] sequence")
2106
2107        if self.closed:
2108            vertices = list(self.vertices)
2109            if value in vertices:
2110                cur_index = vertices.index(value)
2111            else:
2112                if tol is None:
2113                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2114                dist, ind = min(
2115                    [(distance(value, v), i) for i, v in enumerate(vertices)],
2116                    key=lambda x: x[0],
2117                )
2118                if dist < tol:
2119                    cur_index = ind
2120                else:
2121                    return None
2122
2123            shift = index - cur_index
2124            if shift == 0:
2125                return None
2126
2127            if value in vertices:
2128                new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2129            else:
2130                if tol is None:
2131                    tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2132                if distance(value, vertices[cur_index]) < tol:
2133                    new_vertices = vertices[cur_index:] + vertices[:cur_index]
2134                else:
2135                    new_vertices = None
2136            if new_vertices is not None:
2137                res = self.copy()
2138                res[:] = new_vertices
2139            else:
2140                res = None
2141        else:
2142            res = None
2143
2144        return res

If index is not given, the vertex with the given value will be the first index. If index is given, the vertex with the given value will be at the given index. The rest of the indices will be shifted accordingly.

Shape must be closed.

Arguments:
  • index (int): The target index.
  • value (PointType): The vertex to relocate at the given index.
Returns:

Shape: A new shape with the adjusted vertices.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
>>> reordered = rect.reorder_vertices((40, 40))
>>> reordered.vertices
((40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0))

def all_segments( item: Shape | simetri.group.batch.Group, n_round: int = 1, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> list[tuple[Sequence[float], Sequence[float]]]: 
2554def all_segments(
2555    item: Shape | Group,
2556    n_round: int = 1,
2557    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2558    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2559) -> list[tuple[PointType, PointType]]:
2560    """Collect unique line segments from a Shape or Group.
2561
2562    Args:
2563        item: Input shape or group.
2564        n_round: Decimal places used when rounding segment coordinates.
2565        rel_tol: Relative tolerance for segment comparison.
2566        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance for segment comparison.
2567
2568    Returns:
2569        list[LineType]: Deduplicated line segments.
2570
2571    Examples:
2572        >>> tri = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (20, 80)], closed=True)
2573        >>> all_segments(tri)
2574        [((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((20.0, 80.0), (0.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (20.0, 80.0))]
2575    """
2576
2577    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
2578    if isinstance(item, Group):
2579        shapes = item.all_shapes
2580    else:
2581        shapes = [item]
2582    edges = []
2583    for shp in shapes:
2584        edges.extend(shp.edges)
2585    segments = [[p1[:2], p2[:2]] for (p1, p2) in edges]
2586    intersections = all_intersections(segments)
2587
2588    all_segments_ = []
2589    for key, value in intersections[0].items():
2590        segment = segments[key]
2591        points = [x[0] for x in value]
2592        points = remove_duplicate_points(points)
2593        all_segments_.append(multi_split_segment(segment, points))
2594
2595    edges = []
2596    for segs in all_segments_:
2597        for seg in segs:
2598            if distance(*seg) < 0.1:
2599                continue
2600            seg = around((seg), n_round)
2601            seg = (tuple(seg[0]), tuple(seg[1]))
2602            edges.append(seg)
2603
2604    return edges

def clip( item: Shape | simetri.group.batch.Group, clipper: Shape, exclude_clipper: bool = False, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None, merge: bool = True) -> Shape | simetri.group.batch.Group: 
2180def clip(
2181    item: Shape | Group,
2182    clipper: Shape,
2183    exclude_clipper: bool = False,
2184    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2185    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2186    merge: bool = True,
2187) -> Shape | Group:
2188    """Clip a Shape or Group against a closed clipper polygon.
2189
2190    Args:
2191        item: Shape or Group to clip.
2192        clipper: Closed clipping region.
2193        exclude_clipper: If True, treat clipper boundary specially in tests.
2194        rel_tol: Relative intersection tolerance.
2195        abs_tol: Absolute intersection tolerance.
2196        merge: If True, merge clipped fragments via ``merge_shapes``.
2197
2198    Returns:
2199        Shape | Group: Clipped geometry with style copied from ``item``.
2200
2201    Raises:
2202        TypeError: If ``item`` is neither Shape nor Group.
2203
2204    Examples:
2205        >>> subject = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20), (0, 20)], closed=True)
2206        >>> window = sg.Shape([(20, 20), (60, 20), (60, 60), (20, 60)], closed=True)
2207        >>> clip(subject, window)  # doctest: +SKIP
2208    """
2209    if isinstance(item, Group):
2210        return _clip_group(item, clipper, exclude_clipper, rel_tol, abs_tol)
2211    elif isinstance(item, Shape):
2212        clipped_item = _clip_shape(
2213            item,
2214            clipper,
2215            exclude_clipper,
2216            rel_tol,
2217            abs_tol,
2218        )
2219        if clipped_item.type == Types.GROUP:
2220            for clipped_shape in clipped_item:
2221                clipped_shape.copy_style(item)
2222        else:
2223            clipped_item.copy_style(item)
2224
2225        if merge:
2226            clipped_item = clipped_item.merge_shapes()
2227
2228        return clipped_item

def custom_attributes(item: Shape) -> list[str]: 
2339def custom_attributes(item: Shape) -> list[str]:
2340    """Return a list of custom attributes of a Shape or Group instance.
2341
2342    Args:
2343        item (Shape): The Shape or Group instanc
2344    Returns:
2345        list[str]: A list of custom attribute names.
2346
2347    Examples:
2348        >>> poly = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
2349        >>> 'closed' not in custom_attributes(poly)
2350        True
2351    """
2352    dummy = Shape([(0, 0), (1, 0)])
2353    native_attribs = set(dir(dummy))
2354    known_shape_attribs = set(shape_attributes)
2355    custom_attribs = set(dir(item)) - native_attribs - known_shape_attribs
2356
2357    if hasattr(item, "_aliases") and isinstance(item._aliases, dict):
2358        custom_attribs = custom_attribs.difference(set(item._aliases.keys()))
2359
2360    return sorted(custom_attribs)

def get_loop( edges: Sequence[Sequence[Sequence]], start_edge: Sequence[Sequence], ccw: bool = True) -> Shape: 
2607def get_loop(
2608    edges: Sequence[LineType], start_edge: LineType, ccw: bool = True
2609) -> Shape:
2610    """Trace a closed loop through ``edges`` starting from ``start_edge``.
2611
2612    Args:
2613        edges: Segment graph to search.
2614        start_edge: Initial directed edge.
2615        ccw: If True, prefer counterclockwise turns at each node.
2616
2617    Returns:
2618        Closed ``Shape`` when a loop is found, otherwise an open polyline.
2619
2620    Examples:
2621        >>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (40, 40)), ((40, 40), (0, 0))]
2622        >>> loop = get_loop(edges, ((0, 0), (40, 0)))
2623        >>> loop.vertices
2624        ((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0))
2625        >>> loop.closed
2626        True
2627    """
2628    G = nx.Graph()
2629    G.add_edges_from(edges)
2630    if not ccw:
2631        start_edge = (start_edge[1], start_edge[0])
2632
2633    res = [*start_edge]
2634    start_node = start_edge[0]
2635    cur_node = start_edge[1]
2636    cur_edge = start_edge
2637    open_ = True
2638    while open_:
2639        edges_cur_node = set(G.edges(cur_node))
2640        angles = []
2641        for edge in edges_cur_node:
2642            if (edge[1], edge[0]) == cur_edge:
2643                continue
2644            if edge[1] == start_node:
2645                open_ = False
2646                break
2647            angle = angle_between_lines3(*cur_edge, edge[1])
2648            angle = positive_angle(angle)
2649            pi_ = round(pi, 2)
2650            if round(angle, 2) not in (0, -pi_, pi_, 2 * pi_):
2651                angles.append((angle, edge))
2652        if open_:
2653            angles.sort()
2654            if not angles:
2655                break
2656            cur_edge = angles[0][1]
2657            cur_node = cur_edge[1]
2658            res.append(cur_node)
2659
2660    return Shape(res, closed=not (open_))

Trace a closed loop through edges starting from start_edge.

Arguments:
  • edges: Segment graph to search.
  • start_edge: Initial directed edge.
  • ccw: If True, prefer counterclockwise turns at each node.
Returns:

Closed Shape when a loop is found, otherwise an open polyline.

Examples:
>>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (40, 40)), ((40, 40), (0, 0))]
>>> loop = get_loop(edges, ((0, 0), (40, 0)))
>>> loop.vertices

>>> loop.closed
True

2664    item: Shape | Group, edge_index: int, ccw: bool = True

2666    """
2667    Get a sub-region from a shape or group object.
2668    Draw the segments by using canvas.draw_all_segments first to get the indices.
2669    Args:
2670        item Shape | Group: A shape or a group object.
2671        edge_index int: Index of the starting edge of the partition.
2672        ccw bool: If True, the region is formed by looping in

2674
2675    Returns:
2676        The resulting shape object.
2677
2678    Examples:
2679        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)

2686

2688
2689    return get_loop(edges, edges[edge_index], ccw)
